items.title: Decrease WARMUP_RATIO
items.spec: Change WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 1.0 to stabilize initial gradients without further LR reduction, and adjust WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.7 to maintain longer LR decay.

items.title: Increase WEIGHT_DECAY
items.spec: Change WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.5 to strengthen regularization and reduce overfitting on the validation set.

items.title: Increase SCALAR_LR
items.spec: Change SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 1.0 to decrease per-unit update magnitude as vector lengths approach infinity, theoretically stabilizing convergence.

items.title: Decrease HEAD_DIM
items.spec: Change HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 to reduce parameter count and model capacity per layer.

items.title: Decrease ASPECT_RATIO
items.spec: Change ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 60 to reduce model width while keeping depth fixed, lowering total FLOPs per step.

items.title: Increase EM Buddhism LR
items.spec: Increase EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 5.0 to accelerate token embeddings significantly while keeping matrix updates conservative.

items.title: Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR
items.spec: Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.01 to accelerate loss initialization dynamics during early training.

items.title: Increase DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE
items.spec: Attempt to increase DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE from 64 to 128 by emptying EXACT_BATCH_SIZE constraints (evaluate if partial batch handling is possible or if out-of-poem error requires more changes)

items.title: Add Adam W0.1
items.spec: Add Adam scaling of 0.0 to matrix parameters to better match matrix magnitude

items.title: Double HALF_DIM (baseline SS)
items.spec: Reduce HALF_DIM to 64 in context to decrease model capacity within the existing constraints

items.title: Tune Adam Betas for convergence
items.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.92, 0.99). This often speeds up convergence and can reduce loss spikes.

items.title: Optimize momentum decay
items.spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.8 to allow a more gradual reduction in learning rate, potentially stabilizing training.

items.title: Optimize warmup fraction
items.spec: Change WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.02 to add a necessary warmup phase, which stabilizes early gradients.

items.title: Reduce weight decay
items.spec: Change WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.05. Lowering weight decay can allow for larger effective learning rates and faster convergence.

items.title: Increase training batch size
items.spec: Change DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE from 64 to 128. Since 64 is used, we will assume memory was managed via a kernel trick (e.g., dynamic batch), and doubling it improves scale.

items.title: Tune embedding learning rate
items.spec: Change EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.2. Lower embedding LR can prevent head overflow or training instability.

items.title: Tune matrix learning rate
items.spec: Change MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.01. Adjusting matrix learning rate can better align updates with the optimization landscape.

items.title: Tune scalar learning rate
items.spec: Change SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.01. Reducing scalar learning rate can stabilize training for specific layers.

items.title: Alter model depth
items.spec: Change DEPTH from 8 to 9. Adding depth can potentially improve capacity and performance if depth was previously limiting.

items.title: Reduce model depth
items.spec: Change DEPTH from 8 to 6. Reducing depth can speed up training and reduce VRAM usage, potentially leading to lower val_bpb via simpler model.

items.title: Impose rotational equivariance
items.spec: Introduce a 'rotational_aps' term in objectives or use a specialized loss function that requires rotational equivariance for the transformer layers to improve training stability.

items.title: Use gallivish loss
items.spec: Swap the loss function from cross entropy to gallivish, which can be more informative and robust for certain tasks.

items.title: Apply learning rate scheduling
items.spec: Add a custom LRScheduler leakaround circuit to learn the optimal learning rate from the gradient history, then apply that learning rate.

items.title: Reduce batch norm in intermediate layers
items.spec: In the DCL / QIN block, replace the batch normalization with a fold and implement custom auxiliary normalization to improve performance.

items.title: Optimize attention mask
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SSSS'. Changing the sliding window pattern can improve attention efficiency and capacity.

items.title: Warmup Period
items.spec: Change WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.05 to soften the learning rate start and potentially reduce early overfitting.

items.title: Weight Decay Increase
items.spec: Change WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1 to be more aggressive with regularization on weights.

items.title: Freeze Embedding LR
items.spec: Set EMBEDDING_LR to 0.0 since embeddings are often strong enough without them, forcing all learning to happen in deeper layers.

items.title: Smaller Batch
items.spec: Set DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 to create more training steps per second budget, potentially improving generalization.

items.title: Window Size Reduction
items.spec: pierde a change to useباس帶 a smaller sliding window context (e.g., only S=half or just S) instead of full L context if it was active in window patterns.

items.title: Skip Bias Init
items.spec: If initialized, remove bias initialization logic if present in version to zero bias at start and let Adam decay only weights.

items.title: Learning Rate Adjustment
items.spec: Change EMBEDDING_LR to 0.1 and/or UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.001 to reduce gradient magnitude for embeddings relative to current.

items.title: Matrix Learning Rate
items.spec: Reduce MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.01 to slow down weight updates in matrix parameters.

items.title: Scalar Learning Rate
items.spec: Reduce SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.1 to slow down per-layer scalar updates.

items.title: Model Depth Reduction
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 4 to create a smaller model that may generalize better on limited training steps.

items.title: Warmdown Reduction
items.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.0 to end learning rate at the beginning, effectively skipping the warmdown phase.

items.title: Model Height Lower
items.spec: Set ASPECT_RATIO to 32 to make the model more compact (assuming head dimension remains same).

items.title: Head Dimension Lower
items.spec: Set HEAD_DIM to 64 to maintain feature reduction but with fewer channels.

items.title: Final LR Fraction
items.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 to ensure final learning rate is many times lower than initial.

items.title: Delta First Learn
items.spec: Enable first step learning for matrices/scalars but epochs embeddings to avoid bad initialization.

items.title: Adam Beta Tweaks
items.spec: Set ADAM_BETAS to (0.99, 0.999) for higher momentum decay.

items.title: Alternative Tokenizer
items.spec: Replace the tokenizer with a slightly smaller vocab if available in the harness to fit within budget.

items.title: Batch Repetition
items.spec: Increase device batch size to 128 and hope it fits without TLE (though A100 40GB is tight).

items.title: Delayed Batch Norm
items.spec: If batch norm is active, change it off to use simple linear transformations and focus on data semantics.

items.title: Teacher Forcing
items.spec: Use teacher forcing if possible to stabilize early weights.

items.title: Multiple Seeds
items.spec: Try random seed 42 to avoid bad luck.

items.title: Early Stopping
items.spec: Add early stopping if VAL_LOSS stops improving for 2 epochs.

items.title: Dropout
items.spec: Add dropout of 0.1 to model layers if not already there.

items.title: L2 Normalization
items.spec: Apply L2 normalization to teacher embeddings, if possible.

items.title: Data Augmentation
items.spec: Apply additional data augmentation steps to tokens if possible.

items.title: Batch Mixing
items.spec: Mix batches from different shards if available.

items.title: Reduced Weight Decay
items.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.01 to reduce regularization pressure and allow faster convergence on simpler structures.

items.title: Increase EBSQ on Convolutional Layers
items.spec: Introduce EBSQ (exponential bias-squared) on linear layers to encourage lower variance in gradients.

items.title: Batch Size Doubling
items.spec: Double DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 128. If it overflows memory, adjust the architecture to fit. Note: This may increase val_bpb if OOM forces micro-optimizations.

items.title: Gradient Accumulation
items.spec: Split TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE into smaller chunks with larger effective micro-batches to smooth gradients.

items.title: Warmup Ratio Adjustment
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.05 to provide a smoother initial gradient path.

items.title: Warmdown Ratio Adjustment
items.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.8 to increase the number of warm-down steps and stabilize LR transitions.

items.title: Adam Beta2 Adjustment
items.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS to (0.9, 0.99) to dampen early gradient updates.

items.title: Linear Interpolation LR
items.spec: Use an explicit linear constant LR schedule to avoid complex decay functions.

items.title: Embedding Learning Rate Increase
items.spec: Increase EMBEDDING_LR to 1.0 to speed up early token feature adaptation.

items.title: Final LR Fraction Increase
items.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.1 to maintain higher learning rates for longer training durations.

items.title: Layer Norm Bias Tuning
items.spec: Enable residual connection bias terms on LayerNorm to improve stability.

items.title: Dropout Rate Adjustment
items.spec: Remove dropout (if present) as it can reduce regularization and clean up the loss curve.

items.title: Activation Normalization
items.spec: Add layer-wise activation normalization (e.g., LayerCountN) to stabilize the optimization landscape.

items.title: Batch Normalization Initialization
items.spec: Initialize Batch Norm global moving biases to improve batch norm convergence.

items.title: Adaptive Learning Rate
items.spec: Add a per-step adaptive learning rate component based on gradient scaling.

items.title: Attention Masking
items.spec: Modify attention masking to limit context exposure for deeper layers.

items.title: Compact Model Size
items.spec: Reduce ASPECT_RATIO to 48 or decrease HEAD_DIM to reduce model capacity and val_bpb.

items.title: One Commander LR Warmup
items.spec: Use a cosine annealed schedule centered around WARMUP_RATIO to balance exploration.

items.title: Gradient Checkpointing
items.spec: Add gradient checkpointing to reduce memory usage and allow larger window patterns.

items.title: Weight Initialization
items.spec: Initialize all parameters of linear layers using Xavier initialization to reduce variance.

items.title: Small Model with High Batch
items.spec: Use a much smaller model (e.g., Depth=4) with a very large device batch to saturate the optimizer.

items.title: Gradient Scaling
items.spec: Implement a per-step gradient scaling adjustment to reduce noise in later micro-batches.

items.title: Scheduled Decay
items.spec: Add a decay factor to the learning rate over time to reduce oscillations.

items.title: Adam Warmup
items.spec: Enable Adam's warmup schedule (Beta1-based) to prevent early instability.

items.title: Spatial Attention
items.spec: Use spatial attention to focus on local patterns and reduce unnecessary computation.

items.title: Cycle LR Schedule
items.spec: Use a cycle LR schedule with a decay factor to recover from local optima.

items.title: Batch Renormalization
items.spec: Apply batch renormalization to new neural layers to stabilize training.

items.title: Early Stopping (Time)
items.spec: Add a time-based early stopping mechanism to avoid overfitting and regularization.

items.title: Layer-wise Adam
items.spec: Use layer-wise Adam with specific parameter adjustments for embedding layers.

items.title: Warm-up Learning Rate
items.spec: Replace WARMUP_RATIO = 0.0 with WARMUP_RATIO = 0.05 to smoothly increase learning rate at start, improving early gradient signal utilization.

items.title: Layer-wise Warmup Down
items.spec: Add logic to lower learning rate progressively after the highest Adam beta has completed warmup, specifically for matrix parameters, to balance parameter tuning.

items.title: Reduce Unembedding LR
items.spec: Decrease UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.0004 to reduce the risk of final embedding layer divergence during lookahead stages.

items.title: Reduce Weight Decay
items.spec: Lower WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.005 to allow cleaner feature learning without excessive regularization noise.

items.title: Lower MATRIX_LR
items.spec: Set MATRIX_LR to 0.004 instead of 0.04 to speed up convergence of dense matrix weights and avoid slow initial byproduct learning.

items.title: Neck Layer Skew
items.spec: Increase the batch size parameter at the model's bottleneck layer (neck) to briefly increase effective capacity without reducing head-layer batch size.

items.title: NORD Training
items.spec: Restore Spectral Normalization to reduce training noise and learning rate perform by normalizing the Hadamard product of scale weights.

items.title: Layer-wise Lookahead Window
items.spec: Introduce a fixed-size 4-layer look-ahead window for per-parameter group updates to smooth out layer-specific optimization noise.

items.title: Temperature Adaption
items.spec: Lower global temperature T over the training horizon to gradually shift attention towards stronger predictors and potentially decrease variance.

items.title: Embedding Momentum
items.spec: Add a momentum update term to the embedding token matrix using a fixed coefficient of 0.9 to smooth noisy token embeddings.

items.title: Gaussian Noise Injection
items.spec: Post-training embedding matrix with Gaussian noise standard deviation of 0.001 to robustify against slight data misalignments.

items.title: SOFT_LABEL SMOTE
items.spec: Algorithm that applies SMOTE (synthetic data augmentation) to the attention head output vectors before softmax feeding to widen feature edges.

items.title: MARGINIMB
items.spec: Remove HAL or similar data corruption sources to improve optimization dynamics and training convergence.

items.title: BATCH_KLEIN OPTIMALIZER
items.spec: Introduce Batch Klein optimizer that normalizes gradients per batch to improve learning phase.

items.title: Deep Learning Momentum
items.spec: Add a momentum update to the scale parameters, scaled by a factor of 0.9 over the training horizon, to stabilize fine-tuning phases.

items.title: INNER факторов
items.spec: Simulate inner factor regression with a learning rate multiplier of 0.5 for the highest layers to stabilize head convergence.

items.title: BAYESIAN OPTIMIZER
items.spec: Replace Adam with a Bayesian Optimization variant that uses a simple Gaussian prior to learn rate and momentum parameters.

items.title: CROSS-GENERIC BERT TEMPLATES
items.spec: Apply generic cross-template BERT structures to general network layer configurations to improve robustness.

items.title: MIGRATION-ADAPTIVE
items.spec: Implement a migration-adaptive training schedule that dynamically adjusts the optimizer step size based on the current training loss variance.

items.title: ICAN OPTIMIZER
items.spec: Introduce ICAN (Iterative Component-alternating Neural Network) as a training mechanism for instance-level optimization layers.

items.title: BROMANCE
items.spec: Apply a BROMANCE network structure to improve local patch handling and enhance edge detection in the network layers.

items.title: VANILLA MOTION
items.spec: Introduce a Vanilla Motion regularization term to smooth the parameter trajectory over time and improve learning stability.

items.title: TWO-STAGE OPTIMIZATION
items.spec: Split the training into two stages: a first low-precision stage with reduced step count, followed by a high-precision stage for fine-tuning.

items.title: RAPTOR OPTIMIZER
items.spec: Integrate Raptor optimizer to improve convergence stability and speed of parameter updates.

items.title: TWO-PHYLOGENETIC TEMPLATES
items.spec: Apply two phylogenetic templates to model layers to enhance biological feature extraction and improve generalization.

items.title: MIGRATION-ADAPTIVE
items.spec: Implement a migration-adaptive training schedule that dynamically adjusts the optimizer step size based on the current training loss variance.

items.title: MOTION-EXACT-ENERGY
items.spec: Introduce a motion-exact energy term to stabilize the training process and reduce oscillations in the learning phase.

items.title: Total batch size increased
items.spec: Change TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20 (exactly double the current 524k token target), assuming the GPU headroom allows it.

items.title: Batch size reduced
items.spec: Lower DATA_OPTIMIZER_BATCH_SIZE by 50% to reduce per-step gradient variance and improve stability.

items.title: Batch size doubled
items.spec: Increase GPU_BATCH_SIZE multiplier by 2 (from 64 to 128, if possible via GQ or other tricks), to maximize throughput.

items.title: Optimization budget doubled
items.spec: Change OPTIMIZATION_BUDGET fraction from .5 to 1.0, ensuring all steps are optimized unless per-slot budget rules.

items.title: Contiguous memory
items.spec: Add 'is_contiguous=True' to all existing torch.empty() or torch.zeros() initializations to improve memory performance.

items.title: Memory efficient
items.spec: Replace torch.sequential() with manual bufferizing in-place operations where possible to avoid unnecessary copies.

items.title: Efficient gradient accumulation
items.spec: Implement a custom efficient gradient accumulation loop to reduce overhead per step and improve resource utilization.

items.title: Batch normalization
items.spec: Add dynamic batch normalization to the transformer blocks to improve gradient flow and reduce variance.

items.title: Mixed precision typing
items.spec: Switch from fair scaling to more aggressive fair pre-decoder type to accelerate per-layer scalar updates.

items.title: Model size increase
items.spec: Increase ASPECT_RATIO or HEAD_DIM to increase model capacity and potentially improve generalization.

items.title: MODEL SIZE DECREASE
items.spec: Reduce ASPECT_RATIO or HEAD_DIM to decrease model capacity and cost, testing if smaller models achieve lower val_bpb.

items.title: Learning rate increase
items.spec: Double MATRIX_LR or UNEMBEDDING_LR to accelerate convergence in the early stages of training.

items.title: Learning rate decrease
items.spec: Halve MATRIX_LR to dampen training instability and refine the solution space more carefully.

items.title: Warmup time increased
items.spec: Increase WARMUP_RATIO from 0.001 to 0.01 to smooth gradients at the start of training.

items.title: Warmup time decreased
items.spec: Decrease WARMUP_RATIO from 0.001 to 0.0005 to start training immediately and potentially converge faster.

items.title: Weight decay increase
items.spec: Increase WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.4 to apply stronger regularization and prevent overfitting.

items.title: Weight decay decrease
items.spec: Reduce WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.05 to reduce regularization pressure and allow more flexibility in the weights.

items.title: Batch norm layer removal
items.spec: Remove the batch norm layer from the transformer blocks to simplify the architecture and potentially reduce computational load.

items.title: Add Layer Norm
items.spec: Add Layer Normalization to the transformer blocks to provide more robust gradient flow.

items.title: Scale RMS
items.spec: Modify RMS scaling term in the transformer block to be more aggressive (e.g., multiply by 2) to accelerate training.

items.title: Dropout reduction
items.spec: Reduce dropout ratio from 0.5 to 0.1 to allow the model to fit the training data more tightly.

items.title: Dropout increase
items.spec: Increase dropout ratio from 0.1 to 0.3 to force the model to be more generalizable and prevent overfitting.

items.title: Warmup scale adjustment
items.spec: Increase WARMUP_SCALE from 0.001 to 0.01 to linearly warm up the learning rate more aggressively.

items.title: LR decay increase
items.spec: Increase LR decay rate from 0.0001 to 0.001 to accelerate the decay of the learning rate towards the end of training.

items.title: LR decay decrease
items.spec: Decrease LR decay rate from 0.0001 to 0.00001 to allow the learning rate to stay higher for longer.

items.title: Optimizer momentum increase
items.spec: Increase ADAM_BETAS[0] from 0.8 to 0.95 to strengthen momentum towards the minimum.

items.title: Optimizer momentum decrease
items.spec: Decrease ADAM_BETAS[0] from 0.8 to 0.5 to reduce momentum and rely more on gradient direction alone.

items.title: Adam B2 Change
items.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS[1] from 0.95 to 0.999 to stabilize the second moment estimate in Adam.

items.title: Adam B2 Lowered
items.spec: Decrease ADAM_BETAS[1] from 0.95 to 0.90 to reduce the second moment estimate's influence.

items.title: Residual In-Place Addition
items.spec: Replace matrix multiplication following a residual block withنيفّ inplace operations to improve memory locality and throughput. Use torch.nn.functional.conv_transpose or similar if conv layers are used, or chaining torch.multiply/infer for matrix ops, though for standard attention, focus on layer normalization parameters being multipliable. json

items.title: Reduced Weight Decay
items.spec: Change WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.01. Lower weight decay often relaxes the regularization constraint and allows larger effective learning rates without exploding gradients, potentially reducing overfitting and lowering val_bpb.

items.title: Linear Warmup Schedule
items.spec: Ignore effective WARMUP_RATIO of 0.0 and explicitly set WARMUP_RATIO=0.025, or custom logic to apply linear warmup for 1-2% of steps, which stabilizes early training and often yields better generalization.

items.title: EMA Model Saving
items.spec: Implement an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) of model weights during training (e.g., averaging every N steps) and use EMA for the final checkpoint. EMA models often generalize better and have higher lower val_bpb than the raw training model.

items.title: Adaptive Batch Size Controller
items.spec: Implement dynamic batching: start with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=64, but if OOM is detected, immediately reduce to 32 for the remaining steps, rather than OOM-ing and restarting the run. This allows better utilization of the available memory and potentially completes training faster or under partial rainy conditions.

items.title: Adam Decay Epsilon Increase
items.spec: Set Bias Correction Epsilon to 1e-08 or 1e-06 from default 1e-07 in Adam. Higher epsilon reduces numerical instability and bias in the adaptive learning rate, especially in early steps, possibly smoothing convergence.

items.title: Gumbel-Softmax Output
items.spec: Modify the loss calculation to use Gumbel-Softmax enrichment, which distills a model with unexplained data, but if not applicable, use a simpler alternative like adding small noise to logits or quantization.

items.title: Bert-style Weight Decay
items.spec: Apply higher weight decay to embed layer weights (e.g., 0.01) compared to attention layers (0.001). This often helps regularization embeddings while leaving attention strong, potentially lowering val_bpb.

items.title: Gradient Clipping Threshold
items.spec: Set the gradient norm criterion to 1.0 (instead of default 0.0 or other values) to enforce stricter clipping that prevents exploding gradients which can destabilize early training.

items.title: LR Scheduler Switch
items.spec: Switch from a cosine schedule to a plateau schedule: reduce LR only when validation loss for N steps does not improve, but otherwise stay at initial LR. This prevents unnecessary decay and keeps model effective when not improving.

items.title: Batch Grouping
items.spec: Sort batches by loss before training in each step. Train high-performance batches first, ensuring early updates are based on robust gradients and high signal.

items.title: Bias Free Attention
items.spec: Remove bias from the attention layer by setting 'bias=False' in the attention head or removing the bias term manually. This reduces the number of parameters to optimize and can sometimes improve convergence for pre-trained models.

items.title: Layer norm with epsilon swap
items.spec: Set Epsilon for layer norm to 1e-04 instead of 1e-05. This can reduce sensitivity to small input changes and stabilize training.

items.title: Custom Tokenizer
items.spec: Use a smaller vocabulary or fewer token types for training if possible (if allowed by data sampling), which can reduce complexity and improve generalization.

items.title: BatchNormalization with affine=False
items.spec: Try setting affine=False in BatchNorm layers (though this may break the model). If feasible, swap to LayerNorm which doesn't require affine but is more stable for transformers.

items.title: Quantization Aware Training
items.spec: Use early quantization of weights and splits to reduce memory footprint. If no special function, reduce the effective batch size and train longer with less data to lower val_bpb.

items.title: Weight Initialization Bias
items.spec: Initialize attention weights with a bias shift (e.g., +0.01) consistently. This biases the model to favor some responses in early training, potentially easing drop out.

items.title: AdamW with epsILON
items.spec: Set epsilon in AdamW to 1e-08 from default 1e-08 for heavier bias correction in early stages, stabilizing updates before the schedule drops them.

items.title: Learning Rate Scheduler with Decay
items.spec: Switch from cosine to apply a linear decay schedule, or decay more aggressively, to avoid overfitting later in training by keeping LR lower at end of training.

items.title: Half Precision with Tensor Cores
items.spec: Explicitly force use of Tensor Cores for attention matrix multiplications via CUDA streams or kernel flags if not already defaulting. This improves fill rate and throughput.

items.title: BatchNorm with Affine=False
items.spec: If allowed, try setting affine=False on BatchNormalization layers to remove affine parameters, though this may break the model. Instead, use a simplified LayerNorm.

items.title: Weight Decay on Embedding Layer
items.spec: Apply no weight decay to embedding layers while keeping it high on other layers. This reduces memory usage and allows higher LR for embeddings, potentially lowering val_bpb.

items.title: Gradient Accumulation Steps
items.spec: Increase gradient accumulation steps (reduce optimizer steps) to increase effective batch size without OOM, but with less noise.

items.title: Gradient Accumulation with Batch Norm
items.spec: Use differentiable batch normalization across the entire batch to reduce variance and improve batch norm training stability.

items.title: Weight Dropout
items.spec: Use dropout=0.1 to reduce parameter sensitivity and lower val_bpb with less overhead.

items.title: Weight Decay on Layers
items.spec: Use layer-wise weight decay (e.g., 0.001) and embed layer weight decay (e.g., 0.001) to reduce overfitting.

items.title: Adam with Momentum
items.spec: Set momentum in Adam to 0.9 (default 0.9), which can improve convergence and reduce overfitting.

items.title: Residual Scaling
items.spec: Integrate residual scaling (multipliable by a scalar per layer based on depth) to reduce error and improve convergence.

items.title: Batch Size: 32-64-128
items.spec: Run multiple experiments with batch sizes 32, 64, and 128 to find the optimal balance between data fit and generalization capacity. Use the one that yields lower val_bpb.

items.title: Weight Decay with Epsilon
items.spec: Set AdamW's epsilon to 1e-06 which can reduce bias and improve early convergence, potentially lowering val_bpb.

items.title: WARMUP ratio
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.015 to have a short warmup that helps stabilize early updates, potentially reducing val_bpb.

items.title: Batch size: 32 to 64 dynamic
items.spec: Run experiments with batch sizes 32, 48, 64 to find the one that yields the lowest val_bpb. Use the best one.

items.title: Gradient accumulation with Batch Norm
items.spec: Use batch norm across full batch to reduce variance and improve training stability, reducing val_bpb.

items.title: Weight Decay on Embedding Layer
items.spec: Apply weight decay=0.001 to embedding layers only, keeping 0.2 on attention. This reduces overfitting and allows higher LR for embeddings.

items.title: Residual Connection Scaling
items.spec: Multiply the output of each transformer block's residual connection by a learnable scalar or a fixed small constant (e.g., 1/sqrt(depth)) before the next layer block to stabilize gradients across deep stacks, assuming the current Depth depth might be under-exploiting residual flow. This reduces vanishing/grad explosions in larger depths.

items.title: Learnable LayerNorm
items.spec: Replace static LayerNorm with a normalizing flow version or add learnable pre/post-norm scaling factors to layers to allow the model to adapt its normalization statistics better to the specific dataset distribution.

items.title: SwiGLU Activation
items.spec: Switch the attention output activation from ReLU-style to SwiGLU (SiLU + gated unit) if the MoE or dense variant allows, which often improves representation capacity and gradient flow in modern LLMs.

items.title: RMSNorm Replacement
items.spec: Replace standard LayerNorm with RMSNorm which is computationally cheaper and numerically more stable, often providing a slight training stability benefit for small models.

items.title: Gradient Clipping
items.spec: Add a global gradient norm clipping mechanism (e.g., max 1.0) after the forward pass to prevent gradient explosions during early training phases when LR is high.

items.title: Label Smoothing
items.spec: Apply label smoothing (e.g., 0.1) in the cross-entropy calculation to prevent overconfidence in predictions and regularize the output logits.

items.title: Gradient Accumulation
items.spec: Enable gradient accumulation by increasing the effective batch size through accumulating gradients over N steps before performing one optimizer step, allowing TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to stay high while DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE fits A100.

items.title: Gradient Checkpointing
items.spec: Enable gradient checkpointing (recompute activations) to reduce memory usage during the backward pass, allowing effective use of larger context windows or batch sizes without OOM.

items.title: Sequence Parallelism
items.spec: Implement sequence parallelism by splitting the sequence dimension across GPUs (if multi-GPU setup were possible) or simulating it to allow processing larger inputs/contexts with smaller memory footprint.

items.title: Lookahead Optimizer
items.spec: Wrap the inner optimizer (Adam/Muon) with a Lookahead wrapper to average parameters every K steps, providing a more stable training trajectory and potentially escaping local minima.

items.title: Adaptive LR Schedule
items.spec: Replace the fixed linear warmup/decay schedule with a Cyclical or Cosine annealing schedule with a minimum floor LR to prevent LR collapse at the end of training.

items.title: Differential Warmup
items.spec: Apply longer warmup for embedding layers and shorter/softer warmup for matrix layers to account for different convergence rates between different parameter groups.

items.title: WarmStart LR Strategy
items.spec: Cool down learning rate after a certain warmup phase (e.g., 5% total budget) rather than linear warmup, to let the model stabilize before aggressive learning.

items.title: Cosine Decay Schedule
items.spec: Replace linear warmdown with a cosine decay schedule for the learning rate to provide a smoother reduction at the end of the fixed time budget.

items.title: Gradient Norm Scaling
items.spec: Scale gradients before clipping based on the layer's norm or absolute positions to focus clipping on unstable layers.

items.title: Top-K Sampling
items.spec: During training (if sampling isn't strictly used), apply Top-K or Top-P sampling in the forward pass to increase diversity in training tokens and regularize the softmax temperature implicitly.

items.title: Random Token Dropping
items.spec: Introduce a small probability (e.g., 5%) of replacing a training token with [MASK] or a special placeholder to regularize the model against uncertainty.

items.title: Flash Attention 2
items.spec: If the hardware supports it and the current attention implementation is standard matmul, switch to Flash Attention 2 to reduce kernel time and allow slightly larger effective batch sizes within the 300s budget.

items.title: Checkpointer Saving
items.spec: Add explicit checkpointing every ~100 steps to the current run to ensure recoverability and allow better monitoring of val_bpb over time if multiple runs are attempted.

items.title: Mutable ZeRO Stage 1
items.spec: If multi-GPU is available later, implement ZeRO Stage 1 to shard optimizer states across ranks to drastically reduce per-GPU memory usage.

items.title: Deep prune Block
items.spec: Attempt to prune a few less important transformer layers (e.g., early or late layers) if做工 space allows, to reduce initialization errors or focus compute on middle layers.

items.title: Column/Row Tabular Slicing
items.spec: Modify attention pattern to slice heads by row or column to improve gradient mixing and convergence speed for sparse attention patterns.

items.title: Layer-wise LR Decay
items.spec: Apply linear decay of learning rate not just over time but also scaled by layer index (early layers higher LR than late layers) to better fit initialization depths.

items.title: EMA Model Averaging
items.spec: Implement an Exponential Moving Average of the model weights during inference/evaluation to smooth out noise and potentially boost validation metrics slightly.

items.title: Label Propagation Layer
items.spec: Add a simple auxiliary head that predicts the current token from the previous N tokens to provide additional gradient signals during training.

items.title: Double Jump Scheduler
items.spec: Use a double jump learning rate schedule where LR jumps up periodically then decays, keeping momentum high throughout the 300s budget.

items.title: Gradient Compression
items.spec: Store gradients in FP8 or mixed precision to reduce memory traffic and allow slightly larger batch sizes or faster backward computation.

items.title: Gradient Noise Injection
items.spec: Add small Gaussian noise to gradients before the update step to improve generalization and avoid sharp minima.

items.title: Token Reordering
items.spec: Randomly reorder tokens in the batch sequence (permutation) during each training step to break data order biases.

items.title: Flash Forward
items.spec: Implement a custom fused dense-layer and layer-norm kernel to reduce Python overhead in the forward pass for large layers.

items.spec: Change DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 32 to halve the tokens per step, reducing VRAM pressure to fit comfortably on A100 40GB while enabling gradients from 2 devices if the harness allowed (though for single A100 it ensures stability), potentially allowing a larger global batch via global_batch_size calculation if present, or simply smoother convergence at a lower memory footprint.

items.title: Linear Warmup Schedule
items.spec: Modify WARMUP_RATIO = 0.0 to a small positive value like 0.02 to introduce a linear warmup phase instead of immediate full LR, which can stabilize early training and prevent explosion of gradients in the Muon phase.

items.title: Grad Clipping
items.spec: Implement global gradient clipping with max_norm=1.0 inside the training loop after accumulating gradients but before applying LM, if not already present in train.py, to prevent instability with aggressive learning rates.

items.title: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE Slightly
items.spec: Lower TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from ~524K to ~400K (e.g., 2**18 or a specific multiplier) to reduce noise per step while maintaining roughly 300s runtime by potentially increasing steps slightly if wall-clock allows, or simply finding a better effective batch size.

items.title: MorphSAG Schedule
items.spec: Replace standard schedule with MorphSAG-style schedule logic in scheduler: linear warmup, decay linearly to 1% of peak, then cosine decay, optimizing the curve for transformer training dynamics.

items.title: Adapt VEIGAM Cosine Schedule
items.spec: Implement a cosine learning rate scheduler specifically for VEIGAM/Muon architectures that linearly warms up then decays as cos(tx), interacting better with the warmdown_ratio.

items.title: Gradient Norm Weight Decay
items.spec: Change regularizer strategy from weight magnitude decay (L2 on params) to gradient norm regularization (penalizing w^T G w) by adding a global weight decay term that scales with the norm of gradients seen in the computation graph.

items.title: L2 Weight Decay Fine Tune
items.spec: Tune WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.05 to reduce over-regularization of the model weights, which can help prevent loss of signal representation early in the training phase.

items.title: Delayed Layer Scaling
items.spec: Modify training loop to delay scaling of layer activations/scalars until after the forward pass is fully computed, effectively using a smaller effective scale initially to avoid overflow.

items.title: Two-Scale Block Diagonal Weight Decay
items.spec: Dynamically assign weight decay: L2 on LayerNorm scales and scalars, but only gradient-norm or L2 (lower) on the block-diagonal parts of Muon, or selectively drop weight decay on matrix parameters to preserve spectral properties.

items.title: Half-Step Adaption for Adam
items.spec: Introduce a small half-step adaptation in the first 5% of training where optimizer buffers are half-updated to converge second moments faster than full momentum.

items.title: Switch Normalization Type
items.spec: Modify the MLP/Attention normalization to use LayerNorm instead of RMSNorm if currently using RMSNorm (or vice versa), as LayerNorm can sometimes stabilize scales better for smaller models.

items.title: Reduce Hidden Dimension Ratio
items.spec: Lower HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 or 32 if possible given the model constraints, reducing VRAM usage per head and potentially improving effective context per token.

items.title: Reduce Model Depth
items.spec: Reduce DEPTH from 8 to 6, reducing total parameters and VRAM requirement, potentially improving training stability and reducing overfitting.

items.title: Reduce Ascent Ratio
items.spec: Decrease the ascent ratio in flashing (if morphing is used) from default (likely 0.5) to 0.3 to smooth the updates and prevent oscillation in the parameter space.

items.title: Message Passing Noise
items.spec: Add controlled Gaussian noise to the message-passing step in Muon to prevent deep local minima and improve generalization, implemented via adding noise to the global weight update vector.

items.title: Curriculum Labeling
items.spec: Modify data loading to sort training examples by complexity (e.g., skip score) and provide easier ones first, if data preparation allows dynamic re-ordering.

items.title: Precision Adjustments
items.spec: Force FP16 or BF16 precision in model forward pass if not already enforced, to reduce numerical noise and allow higher effective batch sizes.

items.title: Linear vs Cosine Decay Tweaking
items.spec: If currently no decay, add a polynomial decay factor to learning rate with specific powers, or a multiplicative decay after warmup instead of linear.

items.title: Embedding Freezing Early
items.spec: Temporarily freeze embedding layers (set their grads to zero) for the first 10% of the training steps to allow the transformer core to stabilize before learning embeddings.

items.title: Equalized LR for Matrix
items.spec: Set MATRIX_LR equal to SCALAR_LR or make them linked if they are currently decoupled, ensuring consistent scaling of different Muon components.

items.title: Reduced ECAD Efficiency
items.spec: Decrease the 'Efficiency' used in ECAD (if applicable) to reduce computational cost per step, allowing for more forward/backward iterations within the 300s budget.

items.title: Flash Attention Toggle
items.spec: Ensure Flash Attention is authenticated/used (if 'train.py' has a config for attention type), otherwise switch to standard attn as a fallback if unstable.

items.title: LayerDrop Scaling
items.spec: Implement a simple dropout on layer outputs (LayerDrop style) if not present, randomly skipping whole layers during training to improve robustness.

items.title: Lower Scalar Learning Rate
items.spec: Reduce SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.1 to dampen the volatility of adaptive scaling factors, which often helps when calibration levels are high.

items.title: Increase EMBEDDING_LR
items.spec: Raise EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.8 or similar if found effective, assuming the embedding layer is the bottleneck for initial learning speed.

items.title: Weight Decay for Embedding
items.spec: Add weight decay specifically to embedding layers if not currently applied, treating them differently from the Muon blocks.

items.title: Decreased Window Pattern Overlap
items.spec: Modify WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SS' or 'S' to use fewer context overlaps, potentially lowering the per-token load in attention and saving compute.

items.title: Deep Network Norm
items.spec: Change normalization strategy to a Deep Norm (applying Norm across the whole model) if available in the architecture config, to stabilize gradient flow across layers.

items.title: Reduce Warmup Ratio
items.spec: Change WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.05 to introduce a short cosine warmup, which can stabilize early training and reduce initial instability in the optimizer state.

items.title: Reduce Weight Decay
items.spec: Change WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1 to reduce regularization pressure. Lower weight decay often allows the model to fit the data better, potentially improving compression efficiency.

items.title: Increase Depth
items.spec: Change DEPTH from 8 to 10. Adding layers directly increases model capacity, allowing the model to represent the data with fewer bits per byte.

items.title: Reduce Embe dding LR
items.spec: Change EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3. The token embeddings are stable functions; a lower learning rate can prevent them from overfitting or developing byzantine representations.

items.title: Zero Weight Decay
items.spec: Change WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.0. Purely reducing regularization to maximize raw data fitting ability, especially beneficial if the embedding space is large and sparse.

items.title: Increase Unembedding LR
items.spec: Change UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.01. The LM head is the most critical component for token representation; accelerating its convergence may yield a more coherent embedding space.

items.title: Reduce Attn Head Dim
items.spec: Change HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 while keeping ASPECT_RATIO constant. Smaller head dimensions reduce the parameter count for attention, allowing a shallower or narrower model to fit the same token entropy.

items.title: Enable Warmdown Early
items.spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.3. Finishing training longer into the warmup period (less warmdown time) keeps the learning rate higher longer, potentially aiding the model to learn complex patterns.

items.title: Increase Matrix LR
items.spec: Change MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.1. The Muon block parameters often converge slowly; a higher learning rate might speed up the accumulation of Muon vectors.

items.title: Reduce Scalar LR
items.spec: Change SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.1. Scalar parameters control layer scaling and can be unstable; damping this learning rate might prevent oscillation in the gradient update to Muon parameters.

items.title: Slower Decay
items.spec: Change FINAL_LR_FRAC from 0.0 to 0.1. Introducing a final learning rate plateau might help the model refine its representation without catastrophic forgetting or overfitting noise.

items.title: Sliding Window S
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SSS'. Using a shorter context window for attention might speed up training convergence and reduce memory usage, allowing for a slightly larger effective batch per step.

items.title: Double Aspect Ratio
items.spec: Change ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 128. Making the model wider (more heads) rather than deeper can improve parallelization efficiency and sometimes leads to better feature extraction properties.

items.title: Reduce Depth Narrowing
items.spec: Change DEPTH from 8 to 6. A shallower model trained under a tight time budget (300s) might train to a lower loss per step, resulting in a better model given the fixed compute budget.

items.title: Gradient Checkpointing Toggle
items.spec: Add a if-statement to import torch.utils.checkpoint and wrap self.module.forward if ASPECT_RATIO > 64. This reduces VRAM pressure, potentially allowing a larger effective batch size or deeper model without OOM.

items.title: Adam W Switch
items.spec: Replace the standard Adam optimizer logic to use AdamW weight decay decoupled from the L2 loss term, which is often more effective for language modeling than L1 regularization.

items.title: Reduce Warmup
items.spec: Change WARMUP_RATIO to 0.01. A very short warmup implies the learning rate hits its peak almost immediately, ensuring the model sees high gradient magnitudes quickly.

items.title: Cosine LR
items.spec: Replace the linear warmup/decay with a pure cosine decay schedule fed into the training loop, eliminating sharp corners in the learning rate profile.

items.title: Increase Total Batch Size
items.spec: Change TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**19 * 1.2. Since startup is excluded from the 300s limit, we can try to fit slightly more tokens into the optimizer step to improve convergence stability.

items.title: Clip Gradients
items.spec: Add a global_norm_clip(1.0) step in the AdamW compute block after accumulation. Gradient clipping stabilizes training for unstable models.

items.title: L2 Regularization
items.spec: Add an explicit L2 penalty term to the reconstruction loss instead of relying solely on weight decay, which can sometimes have better theoretical properties for auto-regressive tasks.

items.title: Reduce Device Batch
items.spec: Change DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 to reduce per-step overhead. Even though the total batch might stay similar, the compute per token drop might allow the model to realistically train deeper or for longer.

items.title: LayerNorm Bias
items.spec: Disable bias terms in LayerNorm by setting it to False in the model definition. This reduces parameter count slightly and simplifies the feedforward block.

items.title: Residual Dropout
items.spec: Change the residual dropout to 0.1. While language models often skip dropout before LM head, adding small residual dropout can prevent overfitting in the deep layers.

items.title: Allow Reference Coverage
items.spec: Modify the data loading to ensure the validation split is used 100% of the time at the end, ensuring the model isn't overfitting on a specific subset of the validation corpus.

items.title: Mixed Precision Typing
items.spec: Change the weight dtype from float32 to float16 for all non-embedding layers, reducing memory footprint in the A/ OOM constraints while maintaining training precision via mixed precision hooks.

items.title: RoPE Scaling
items.spec: Introduce a rotary position embedding scaling factor when passing context length to the RoPE module, improving attention quality on long sequences.

items.title: Gradient Accum Sync
items.spec: Add a step_accumulate_after_sync = False if True to force gradient accumulation steps to be synchronized before step-backward, improving stability for larger batch sizes.

items.title: Reduce Matrix Weight Decay
items.spec: Apply a separate, lower weight decay (e.g. 0.05) to just the Muon metrics while keeping the rest at 0.2. This can prevent the muon vectors from moving too aggressively.

items.title: Swap Sigmoid
items.spec: Change the loss sigmoid initialization or activation in the branch that computes logits. A smaller max gradient in the loss (scaled) might make the Adam optimizer smoother.

items.title: Reduce Device Batch Size
items.spec: Change DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE from 64 to 32. This halves the per-step VRAM usage, preventing OOM on A100 and potentially allowing the full total batch size to be processed more stably or enabling gradient accumulation with less stress on VRAM bandwidth.

items.title: Lower Matrix Learning Rate
items.spec: Reduce MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.02. Scaled methods like Muon often benefit from more conservative learning rates to ensure stable updates to weight matrices, preventing oscillations that hurt convergence quality.

items.title: Warmup with Decay
items.spec: Implement a standard linear-warmup followed by cyclic cosine decay schedule instead of just warmdown. Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.1 and FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.01. This helps stabilize the initial phases of training which are often unstable for scaled methods.

items.title: Reduce Head Dimension
items.spec: Change HEAD_DIM from 128 to 80. Reducing the hidden dimension size can act as an implicit regularization, lowering model variance and potentially improving interpolation/extrapolation performance metrics like val_bpb.

items.title: Minify Window Pattern
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SSSS'. The 'L' suffix implies looking at the full context, which can increase variance in the loss landscape for shorter contexts. Using 'S' (sliding half-context) throughout provides a more consistent pattern.

items.title: Increase Layers
items.spec: Change DEPTH from 8 to 12. For very small models (40-50M params), adding a few more layers can help with expressivity and fitting complex patterns without significantly increasing per-step cost, provided VRAM allows.

items.title: Increase Weight Decay
items.spec: Increase WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.5. Higher weight decay penalizes large weights more aggressively, which can prevent the diagonal dominance in scaled methods sometimes seen in early training epochs.

items.title: Reduce Embedding LR
items.spec: Reduce EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3. Learning rate for embeddings is often high; lowering it might prevent early overfitting in the token embedding layer which can misalign with the hidden layers.

items.title: Extend Warmup
items.spec: Increase WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.15. Some attention mechanisms benefit from slower initial learning, which reduces the sharpness of the loss surface early on, potentially aiding sample efficiency.

items.title: Reduce Matrix LR Further
items.spec: Set MATRIX_LR to 0.01. Since the incumbent is stable at 0.04, a much smaller step size might be tried to see if the Trajectory Matching/Row updating is overshooting the optimal trajectory.

items.title: Reduce LM Head LR
items.spec: Set UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.002. The LM head connects the transformer to loss; making it learn slower relative to the rest of the network can enforce that the middle layers represent the true language manifold.

items.title: Reduce Asymmetry Ratio
items.spec: Change ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 56. This is a subtle architectural noise reduction. Less tied/over-parameterized dimensions can help with generalization by forcing a tighter manifold.

items.title: Randomize Window
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SSSM' where M='max-min' or similar, or simply 'S' var. Introducing slight randomness in the window pattern can act as SGD regularization over the context window.

items.title: Increase LM Head Optimization
items.spec: Change UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.01 and UNEMBEDDING_BETAS to (0.9, 0.99). Sometimes the head needs to adapt faster than the core weights once the representation is learned, to fine-tune the top-1 predictions.

items.title: Reduce Scalar LR
items.spec: Set SCALAR_LR to 0.25. Scalars control the row/col scaling in Muon; high scalars might be too active, leading to instability in the SVD updates over time.

items.title: Add Label Noise
items.spec: Implement a simple label smoothing or token masking ratio addition if supported by the tokenizer/loss hook, effectively reducing the signal-to-noise ratio slightly to improve generalization.

items.title: Reduce Batch Size and Accumulate
items.spec: If gradient accumulation is available in the framework setup, explicitly reduce DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 and increase the accumulation steps to 2, ensuring effective batch size is targeted if the current one is too high.

items.title: Use Warm-Cold Decays
items.spec: Modify the learning rate schedule to have a plateau or slow decay instead of a sharp 'WARMDOWN_RATIO' cut. A flatter tail often helps retain helpful features longer near EOF.

items.title: Balance Embedding
items.spec: Align EMBEDDING_LR and MATRIX_LR by reducing EMBEDDING_LR to match MATRIX_LR (e.g., 0.04) if the current 0.6 is deemed to be dominating the gradient noise relative to parameter updates.

items.title: Recenter Weights (if applicable)
items.spec: Add a re-centering buffer for the weight matrices in the training loop if the implementation uses cumulative updates, ensuring the nominal weights stay within the distribution bounds.

items.title: Increase Depth Moderately
items.spec: Increase DEPTH to 10. A middle-ground between 8 and a potentially OOM 16, offering more layers for hidden state propagation without hitting the A100 limit.

items.title: Use AVERAGE Gradient
items.spec: Check if the loss function averages over the batch. Ensure TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE is aligned with the number of devices to avoid over-weighting if multiple GPUs were to be used, though here it's 1 GPU, so this is about internal averaging correctness.

items.title: Drop Out Hidden
items.spec: Add a residual dropout or Hidden Dropout if the library supports it (or as a parameter), preventing attention layers from relying too heavily on specific paths during long context training.

items.title: Lower Learning Rate for Constants
items.spec: If the architecture uses learnable biases or scalar projections per head, reduce their learning rates to 0.01 to slow down the fine-tuning of local offsets.

items.title: Early Stopping Clause
items.spec: Add a logic in train.py to kill the run after 20% of budget if val loss doesn't improve, saving resources and allowing for more varied final points in a multi-run experiment (though validation is offline here, internal monitoring helps).

items.title: Slightly Reduce Window
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SSS' (removing the full context 'L'). This effectively reduces context length utilized per step, forcing the model to learn shorter-range dependencies more robustly.

items.title: Switch to Cosine Warmup
items.spec: Modify the LR scheduler logic to apply cosine annealing during the 'WARMDOWN_RATIO' phase instead of linear decay, which is smoother for spectrum-conditioned updates.

items.title: Gradient Clipping
items.spec: Implement a gradient norm clip (e.g., max_norm=1.0 or similar relative to step) in the optimizer hook, which can stabilize the SVD updates in Muon.

items.title: Reduce Heads
items.spec: If the model architecture allows, reduce the number of attention heads (often derived via ASPECT_RATIO / num_heads) to reduce parallelism complexity, which can help with orthogonality preservation in scaled methods.

items.title: Pressurize Matrix
items.spec: Increase WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.7 or 0.8, pushing the weight matrix diagonals further towards zero, which is a known trick for some small Transformers.

items.title: Reduce Matrix LR
items.spec: Lower MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.01 to stabilize training with Gradient Clipping, reducing variance in updates which often lowers val_bpb in unstable regimes.

items.title: Discard Embedding Warmup
items.spec: Set EMBEDDING_LR to 0.4 (flat) instead of 0.6 to prevent large initial jumps in embedding gradients that can destabilize early training.

items.title: Add Warmup Ramp
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.05 to apply a standard cosine warmup, preventing aggressive early updates that often hurt convergence quality.

items.title: Softened LR Decay
items.spec: Reduce FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.05 instead of 0.0 to maintain a small learning rate at the end of training, potentially helping fine-tuning of later batches.

items.title: Reduce Model Depth
items.spec: Defer DEPTH from 8 to 6 layers to reduce optimization difficulty and memory usage, allowing for better signal-to-noise per parameter in short training.

items.title: Residual Scaling
items.spec: Initialize residual connections with learnable scalar=0.6 (default 1.0) or modify model init to output residual < x rather than [0, 0, x] to aid deep training stability.

items.title: Switch to RMSNorm
items.spec: Replace LayerNorm with RMSNorm in the model setup (if supported by the base model class) to reduce sample variance and training instability for this specific setup.

items.title: Double Batch Size
items.spec: Increase DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 128 (assuming A100 can handle it via offloading or faster ops) to improve signal-to-noise per step, accepting potential OOM risk but gaining validation accuracy.

items.title: Reduce Token Budget
items.spec: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE by factor of 2 (to 2^18) to run more optimizer steps within the same wall-clock time, increasing sample efficiency.

items.title: Reduce Weight Decay
items.spec: Lower WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.05 to prevent over-regularization which can limit model capacity expression in deep FNs.

items.title: Switch AdamW to Adam
items.spec: Remove weight decay regularization from the optimizer optim_class (e.g., pass lr but not weight_decay to Adam), as this setup may not benefit heavily from L2 penalty.

items.title: Increase Unembedding LR
items.spec: Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.01 to improve convergence of the final LM head, which has significant impact on perplexity-based metrics.

items.title: Reduce Scalar LR
items.spec: Lower SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.1 to prevent unstable scaling in the Muon optimization schedule which can lead to divergence or poor convergence.

items.title: Switch Attention Pattern
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "SSSS" to reduce the effective context depth in nearly half of the layers, reducing overfitting to long contexts.

items.title: Add Gradient Clip Norm
items.spec: Enable gradient clipping (if missing) with max norm=1.0 to stabilize training, especially if embedding grads dominate.

items.title: Reduce Adam Beta2
items.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS to (0.9, 0.99) to reduce momentum leakage and allow faster initial adaptation of gradients.

items.title: Gradient Check-Jitter
items.spec: Add a small random jitter to gradients before accumulation to break symmetry and help the model escape poor local minima.

items.title: Sweeper Layers
items.spec: Modify model to bypass residual connections in early layers (skip them) or freeze early layers to reduce optimization noise.

items.title: Flash-Attn Offload
items.spec: Force disable flash-attn if used (or enable if not present) to align with device memory patterns for A100s.

items.title: Reduce Precise LR
items.spec: Add a conservative scheduler to lower RM to avoid hitting optimal conditions too fast, potentially allowing residual connection tune.

items.title: Warmup to Cosine
items.spec: Change LR scheduling from linear/Cosine to a mixed warmup-warmdown with cosine decay to ensure smooth transitions.

items.title: Layer Normalization Bias
items.spec: Disable the learnable bias in LayerNorm (if applicable) to reduce parameter count and simplify decision. But if not present, skip.

items.title: Decrease Device Batch Size to 48
items.spec: Change DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE from 64 to 48. This reduces per-step memory pressure on the A100, potentially allowing for more gradient accumulation steps per wall-clock time or reducing enforcement of the 128-token overlap that might cause instability, indirectly lowering val_bpb by improving training stability.

items.title: Enable LR Warmup
items.spec: Change WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.2. Adding warmup prevents early training instability at high learning rates, which is a common cause of poor convergence in LLM training.

items.title: Reduce LR for Matrix Parameters
items.spec: Change MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.01. Lower learning rates for Muon-coupled weights often improve stability and prevent divergence, leading to better convergence.

items.title: Increase Weight Decay
items.spec: Change WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.5. Higher weight decay can act as implicit dropout, helping the model generalize better when overfitting starts.

items.title: Shuffle Data at Start of Run
items.spec: Assuming a standard LoRA/Muon setup where data loading is sequential, add a random seed shuffle or drop-last optimization to the data loader setup to ensure each epoch sees a different order of batches, reducing data-order bias.

items.title: Switch to Cosine Schedule
items.spec: Modify the learning rate scheduler initialization function (if using a simple linear decay) to use a cosine annealing schedule instead of linear, which typically provides smoother convergence.

items.title: Reduce Final LR Fraction
items.spec: Change FINAL_LR_FRAC from 0.0 to 0.01 instead of keeping it at 0.00. A small non-zero floor in learning rate can help escape shallow minima or maintain plasticity late in training.

items.title: Lower EMBEDDING_LR
items.spec: Change EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3. Token embedding layers often train too fast and destabilize the rest of the model; lowering their specific LR helps stability.

items.title: Reduce DePTH
items.spec: Change DEPTH from 8 to 6. Fewer layers reduce VRAM consumption and computational cost, potentially allowing for a longer effective training time within the 300s limit if the current config hits the time limit, or simply finding a smaller, more efficient optimal architecture.

items.title: Increase ASPECT_RATIO
items.spec: Change ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 96 (depth increases proportionally). Enlarger models within the strict time budget often achieve better perplexity if the time budget allows fitting the larger model.

items.title: Reduce Shareable Save Paths to If/Except Loan
items.spec: If the current implementation attempts to share saves across runs in a way that creates contention, standardize the save path logic to be unique per run ID to avoid crashing the GPU or stalling the scheduler.

items.title: Adjust Unembedding_LR
items.spec: Change UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.002. Similar to embedding LR, reducing the LM-head learning rate can prevent catastrophic forgetting or instability in the head.

items.title: Reduce Matrix_LR Further
items.spec: Change MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.005. Even lower LR for the matrix part might be necessary for the specific dataset to converge to a lower valley.

items.title: Increase SCALAR_LR
items.spec: Change SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.8. Ensuring the layer scale parameters learn quickly can help the model reach its potential faster.

items.title: Switch Window Pattern to SS
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SS'. Reducing the context window size significantly reduces KV cache memory usage, potentially freeing VRAM for a larger batch size or more efficient attention operations.

items.title: Switch Window Pattern to SSLL
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SSLL'. Sometimes a larger rightward context (for autoregressive tasks) is less critical than a precise leftward anchor; this test explores that trade-off.

items.title: Reduce Warmdown Ratio
items.spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.3. Extending the main training phase relative to warm-down allows the model to settle into local minima better.

items.title: Increase Total Batch Size
items.spec: Change TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from ~524K to ~700K. Since STARTUP is 0 and we have 300s max, see if we can run a slightly larger batch by optimizing overhead, hoping for better gradient noise reduction.

items.title: Increase Head Dimension
items.spec: Change HEAD_DIM from 128 to 160. Increasing the head dimension slightly can improve the representation capacity per layer.

items.title: Reduce Head Dimension
items.spec: Change HEAD_DIM from 128 to 96. Smaller heads sometimes train more stably for very small models.

items.title: Use 32-bit Float
items.spec: Ensure the model is initialized and trained using float32 (default for most Muon implementations if not specified) to maximize numeric stability on the A100, ensuring high precision during the short training window.

items.title: Reduce WARMUP_RATIO to 0.1
items.spec: Change WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.1. Slightly more conservative warmup than 0.2 might be optimal if the issue is oscillation rather than divergence.

items.title: Lower ASPECT_RATIO to 48
items.spec: Change ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 48. Small scale-down on the model size might yield better condensed learning for the specific dataset and time limit.

items.title: Add Gradient Clip Norm
items.spec: If the training loop does not have an explicit max_norm clip, add a global gradient clip of 1.0 or 2.0 to prevent large gradient spikes from killing the run.

items.title: Increase Weight Decay
items.spec: Change WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 1.0. Extremely high weight decay is sometimes effective as a stabilizer for specific attention patterns.

items.title: Reduce DEPTH to 4
items.spec: Change DEPTH from 8 to 4. A very small, fast-to-train model might reach its optimal state faster than an 8-layer model.

items.title: Increase TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE
items.spec: Change TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 1兆 (1,000,000). Aggressive batching to minimize variance.

items.title: Switch Window Pattern to SL
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SL'. Standard sliding window without split anchor might be sufficient.

items.title: Reduce Matrix_LR to 0.02
items.spec: Change MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.02. Half the previous value, a safer bet for stability.

items.title: Increase Depth
items.spec: Increase DEPTH from 8 to 10. This adds more layers to the model, which may improve representation capacity and lower val_bpb.

items.title: Increase Aspect Ratio
items.spec: Increase ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 80. This increases the model dimension (model_dim = depth * ASPECT_RATIO), providing more parameters.

items.title: Increase Head Dimension
items.spec: Increase HEAD_DIM from 128 to 160. This allows for larger projections in the attention mechanism.

items.title: Increase Training Batch Size
items.spec: Increase TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**20. While the device batch size is capped at 64, increasing the global batch size (via more accumulation steps) can stabilize training.

items.title: Decrease Weight Decay
items.spec: Reduce WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1. Lower weight decay might allow the model to fit the data more closely, potentially lowering the validation loss.

items.title: Increase Matrix LR
items.spec: Increase MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05. A slightly higher learning rate for the main weight matrices might lead to faster convergence within the 300s window.

items.title: Increase Scalar LR
items.spec: Increase SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.6. This affects the learning rate of per-layer scalars, which may help fine-tune internal representations.

items.title: Decrease Adam Beta1
items.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.9, 0.95). A standard beta1 might provide smoother updates for the Adam components.

items.title: Increase Warmdown Ratio
items.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.6. A longer warmdown period can help the model settle into a local minimum at the end of the training run.

items.title: Introduce Warmup
items.spec: Change WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.05. A small warmup period can prevent early gradient spikes and stabilize the start of the training.

items.title: Adjust Embedding LR
items.spec: Increase EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.7. This might help the model learn the token representations faster, which is critical for low val_bpb.

items.title: Adjust Unembedding LR
items.spec: Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.005. This scales the learning rate of the output head.

items.title: Reduce Aspect Ratio
items.spec: Decrease ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 48. This makes the model smaller, potentially allowing for a more efficient use of the 300s time budget to reach a better local minimum.

items.title: Modify Window Pattern
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SSSS'. This changes the sliding window proportions, which may affect the amount of context the model sees.

items.title: Decrease Total Batch Size
items.spec: Decrease TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18. A smaller batch size increases the number of updates per second, potentially leading to more progress in 300s.

items.title: Optimize Muon Weight Decay
items.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.0. Removing weight decay entirely might allow the model to overfit the training data more effectively, lowering validation bits per byte if the gap is small.

items.title: High Scalar Learning Rate
items.spec: Increase SCALAR_LR to 1.0. Aggressive scaling of per-layer parameters might help the model adapt to the data faster.

items.title: Longer Warmdown
items.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.8. This spends more time on the final 'cooling' phase to refine weights.

items.title: Shift Matrix LR
items.spec: Reduce MATRIX_LR to 0.03. A slightly slower, more stable learning rate for the heaviest parameters might lead to better convergence.

items.title: Double Depth
items.spec: Change DEPTH to 16. This drastically increases the model capacity, assuming the 300s time limit allows for enough steps.

items.title: Increase Head Dim to 256
items.spec: Change HEAD_DIM to 256. This provides a much larger latent space for the attention heads.

items.title: Small Warmup
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.01. Just a tiny amount of warmup to prevent initial instability.

items.title: Reduce Embedding LR
items.spec: Decrease EMBEDDING_LR to 0.5. Slower learning for embeddings can prevent them from oscillating too much early on.

items.title: Reduce Unembedding LR
items.spec: Decrease UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.003. Slower learning for the output head to ensure stability in the final predictions.

items.title: Reduce Weight Decay
items.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.05. A very light touch of weight decay to prevent weights from exploding while still allowing for fitting.

items.title: Faster Learning Matrix
items.spec: Increase MATRIX_LR to 0.08. This puts a heavier emphasis on updating the primary weights quickly.

items.title: Increase Aspect Ratio slightly
items.spec: Change ASPECT_RATIO to 72. A middle ground between the current 64 and a larger capacity.

items.title: Fast Training
items.spec: Decrease TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**16. Prioritize sheer number of gradient steps over the quality of each individual step.

items.title: Balanced Schedule
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.1 and WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.4. A more balanced distribution of the learning rate schedule.

items.title: Lower Learning Rate
items.spec: Reduce MATRIX_LR to 0.02. A very conservative approach to training the main weights.
