items.title: Disable Warmup
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.0 to 0.1. Many transformers benefit from a gradual learning rate increase to stabilize the start of training better than immediate full learning rate.

items.title: Reduce Warmdown Aggressiveness
items.spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.2 or 0.3. A more gradual decay at the end of training helps retain learned nuances and improves generalization (val_bpb).

items.title: Increase EMBEDDING_LR
items.spec: Set EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.8 or 0.9. Token embeddings often act as a projector and may benefit from a higher learning rate matrix to adapt quickly to the corpus.

items.title: Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR
items.spec: Set UNEMMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.01 or 0.02. The LM head learns distribution directly; a higher LR here can accelerate convergence to the target vocabulary distribution.

items.title: Decrease MATRIX_LR
items.spec: Set MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.02. For matrices updated via Muon (with diagonal pre-conditioning), a lower LR often provides smoother convergence and prevents overshooting critical regions.

items.title: Increase Matrix LR Linearly
items.spec: Modify the learning rate schedule logic to scale MATRIX_LR as `base_lr * (0.6 + 0.4 * progress)`. Increasing the matrix step size in the middle of training can accelerate decorrelation of embeddings.

items.title: Enable Cosine LR Decay
items.spec: Replace the linear warmdown logic (WARMDOWN_RATIO) with a cosine annealing scheduler function within the training loop, which typically yields better final model quality than linear decay.

items.title: Increase Weight Decay
items.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.5 or 1.0 for the Muon angles. Higher weight decay on the preconditioner's angles often improves robustness to overfitting on limited data.

items.title: Reduce Total Batch Size
items.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**17 or 2**18. A smaller per-step batch size can reduce noise variance in the gradient estimates relative to fixed compute time, potentially improving optimization landscape navigation.

items.title: Disable Sliding Window
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'FF' (Full context). Increasing context width allows the model to see more causal dependencies per forward pass, potentially lowering BOS token loss.

items.title: Narrow Head Dimension
items.spec: Change HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 or 96. Reducing head size increases the number of heads for the same computational budget (depth * aspect_ratio = dims), improving positional encoding learning.

items.title: Increase Model Depth
items.spec: Change DEPTH from 8 to 10 or 12. Adding more layers increases representational capacity within the fixed compute budget, allowing the model to capture deeper linguistic patterns.

items.title: Lone Layer Sliding Window
items.spec: Modify the forward pass to apply sliding window masking to all layers except the very last one, keeping full context at the accumulation layer for token prediction.

items.title: Modified Muon Gradient Noise
items.spec: Add logic to the Muon step to add small Gaussian noise to the weight updates proportional to the gradient norm before applying the preconditioner, acting as explicit stochastic regularization.

items.title: Reduce Start of Warmup
items.spec: If WARMUP is implemented, shift the warmup start earlier or make the slope less steep to avoid early instability in the pre-training phase.

items.title: Use Weight Norm
items.spec: Wrap the attention matrices (Q, K, V) and FFW layers in a WeightNorm wrapper before training to act as an implicit gradient normalization, stabilizing the training dynamics.

items.title: Gradient Clipping
items.spec: Implement global gradient norm clipping (e.g., max_norm 2.0) in the optimizer step to prevent exploding gradients during the early epochs of training.

items.title: Increase Depth Linearly
items.spec: Change DEPTH to 8, but implement the architecture such that ASPECT_RATIO expands slightly at deeper layers as budget permits in implementation logic.

items.title: Reduce Embedding Dim
items.spec: Change ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 40 or 48. Reducing embedding dimension forces the model to be more efficient with representations, potentially helping if data is sparse.

items.title: Per-Layer LR Scaling
items.spec: Modify the training loop to assign a slightly lower learning rate to the LM head (LM_HEAD_LR = MATRIX_LR * 0.5) compared to the rest of the matrix trainables.

items.title: Scalar LR Reducing
items.spec: Reduce SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.2. High-frequency token probability log-probs often react differently than position/embedding formats; dampening scalars can smooth the probability landscape.

items.title: Dynamic Batch Size
items.spec: Implement a batch size that starts at 32 and scales to 64(128) as VRAM availability and gradient stability permit during the run, rather than fixing it at 64.

items.title: Re-implement Warmup Linear
items.spec: Ensure the warmup phases use a strictly linear ramp: start at 0, reach max at WARMUP_EPOCHS, hold, then linear down. smoother transitions often help convergence.

items.title: Dropout Activation
items.spec: Add a ReLU or GELU activation before the residual connection in the attention block if not already present, increasing non-linearity and data flow.

items.title: Switch to Deep-Compound
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN to a compound strategy 'FX' (Full context for tokens, Sliding for intermediate) to reduce long-context dependency errors.

items.title: Cosine Decay for All
items.spec: Apply cosine decay to both EMBEDDING_LR and MATRIX_LR separately, rather than a unified scalar schedule, fine-tuning their convergence speeds.

items.title: Warmup + Cosine Combo
items.spec: Replace linear warmup with 't-annealing' (linear warmup followed immediately by cosine decay) which is a standard SOTA practice for similar architectures.

items.title: Targeted LR for LM Head
items.spec: explore setting UNEMBEDDING_LR slightly higher than SCALAR_LR to encourage the head to capture distributional features faster than the context modeling layers.

items.title: LayerNorm Scaling
items.spec: Introduce a learnable gain parameter (gamma) to the LayerNorm layers, initialized to 1.0, and multiply the normalized output by this gain. This can help stabilize training and potentially improve representation.

items.title: Rotary Embeddings (RoPE)
items.spec: Replace standard absolute positional embeddings (if any) or simple index-based methods with Rotary Positional Embeddings (RoPE) to better capture relative distances.

items.title: Stochastic Depth
items.spec: Implement Stochastic Depth (DropPath) to randomly skip entire transformer blocks during training, increasing regularization and helping with convergence.

items.title: Weight Decay for Adam
items.spec: Apply weight decay to the Adam optimizer's parameters (EMBEDDING_LR, UNEMBEDDING_LR, SCALAR_LR) instead of just the Muon optimizer's parameters.

items.title: Cosine Annealing with Restarts
items.spec: Change the LR schedule from a simple linear warmup/warmdown to a Cosine Annealing schedule with a restart every 100 steps.

items.title: RMSNorm
items.spec: Replace LayerNorm with RMSNorm in all transformer blocks, as it often provides faster convergence and better stability for large models.

items.title: Grouped Query Attention (GQA)
items.spec: Implement GQA by reducing the number of key/value heads relative to the number of query heads, which can speed up inference and improve memory efficiency.

items.title: Increased Weight Decay
items.spec: Increase the WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.4 for the Muon optimizer to enforce stronger sparsity and regularization.

items.title: Switch to AdamW
items.spec: Replace the standard Adam optimizer for embedding and unembedding layers with AdamW, which decouples weight decay from the gradient update.

items.title: Pre-LayerNorm
items.spec: Ensure the architecture uses Pre-LayerNorm (applying Norm before the attention/FFN blocks) rather than Post-LayerNorm for improved gradient flow.

items.title: Flash Attention 2
items.spec: Incorporate Flash Attention 2 kernels (if available/compatible) to optimize the memory-bandwidth bottleneck of the attention mechanism.

items.title: Dimension Balancing
items.spec: Adjust the ASPECT_RATIO such that the hidden dimension is a power of 2 (e.g., 1024, 2048) to align better with GPU memory layouts.

items.title: Gradient Clipping
items.spec: Add a global gradient norm clipping step (e.g., max_norm=1.0) to the training loop to prevent exploding gradients.

items.title: Learning Rate Scaling
items.spec: Scale the initial learning rates (MATRIX_LR, etc.) by the square root of the TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to maintain consistency across different batch sizes.

items.title: FFN Expansion Factor
items.spec: Introduce a hyperparameter to control the expansion factor of the Feed-Forward Network (e.g., 4x hidden_dim).

items.title: Warmup Duration
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.1 to provide a smoother start for the optimizer, preventing early divergence.

items.title: Mixed Precision (BF16)
items.spec: Enable automatic mixed precision (AMP) using BF16 for all matrix multiplications to speed up training and reduce VRAM usage.

items.title: Head Dim Optimization
items.spec: Set HEAD_DIM to 64 (instead of 128) to increase the number of attention heads, potentially improving multi-head diversity.

items.title: Weight Initialization
items.spec: Use a Xavier or Kaiming initialization specifically tuned for the RoPE and LayerNorm layers to improve starting point variance.

items.title: Gradient Accumulation
items.spec: Implement gradient accumulation to simulate a larger effective batch size if DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE is restricted by memory.

items.title: Layer Scaling
items.spec: Multiply the output of the attention scores by the square root of the head dimension (standard in Attention is All You Need).

items.title: Switch to AdaFactor
items.spec: Replace Adam and Muon with a factored optimizer like AdaFactor to reduce memory footprint while maintaining adaptive learning rates.

items.title: Deep Residual Connections
items.spec: Ensure each transformer block uses a residual connection (x + sublayer(x)) to facilitate deeper gradient flow.

items.title: Learning Rate Decay
items.spec: Introduce a 0.95 multiplier to the learning rate every 50 steps during the warmdown phase.

items.title: Activation Function Swap
items.spec: Replace ReLU in the Feed-Forward Network with GELU or SiLU (Swish) to improve non-linearity smoothness.

items.title: Optimizer Momentum
items.spec: Increase the beta1 parameter in ADAM_BETAS from 0.8 to 0.9 to increase the influence of past gradients.

items.title: Dimension Reduction
items.spec: Reduce the total model size by decreasing the DEPTH from 8 to 6, while slightly increasing ASPECT_RATIO to keep parameter count similar.

items.title: Lookahead Optimizer
items.spec: Wrap the existing optimizers in a Lookahead wrapper to improve convergence stability.

items.title: Weight Decay for Scalars
items.spec: Explicitly set weight decay for the scalar parameters to 0.1 to prevent them from vanishing.

items.title: Sequence Length Penalty
items.spec: Implement a simple weight penalty for longer sequences in the loss function to encourage more concise generation.

items.title: Tune Weight Decay for Muon
items.spec: Change WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.05 to reduce regularization strength and see if it improves val_bpb, effectively halving the weight penalty applied to matrix parameters.

items.title: Increase Matrix Learning Rate
items.spec: Increase MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.1 to accelerate the movement of the gradient-free component in Muon optimization, potentially reaching minima faster within the 300s budget.

items.title: Enable Warmup
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.1 (10% of time) to gradually ramp up the learning rate, reducing training instability at the start of the 300s run.

items.title: Reduce Embedding LR
items.spec: Lower EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3 to stabilize the training of token embeddings, which are sensitive to high learning rates.

items.title: Deepen Model Architecture
items.spec: Increase DEPTH from 8 to 10 layers slightly expanding model capacity, potentially capturing more complex patterns in the validation set.

items.title: Narrow Model Width
items.spec: Decrease ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 48 to reduce VPB (val bits per byte) via a smaller, potentially over-regularized model that fits well within memory constraints.

items.title: Adopt Full Attention
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'FF' (full) to let the model see the entire context window, potentially improving performance if the current sparse attention is too restrictive.

items.title: Reduce Final LR Fraction
items.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.01 (1%) to ensure the learning rate decays more aggressively near the end of the 300s budget, preventing divergence.

items.title: Tune LM-Head LR
items.spec: Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.01, allowing the language model head to adapt faster to the new distribution created by the embedding updates.

items.title: Shorten Warmdown
items.spec: Reduce WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.25, keeping the learning rate higher for longer to better utilize the 300s training budget.

items.title: Increase Depth to 12
items.spec: Bump DEPTH up to 12 to significantly increase model capacity, assuming the A100 memory can handle the slightly larger hidden layer sizes through the batch size reduction.

items.title: Blend Optimizers: AdamW
items.spec: Replace the custom train loop or optimizer setup to use a standard AdamW scheduler with global step decay if the current Muon setup is not converging well, though this requires significant loop rewriting so stick to parameter tuning first.

items.title: Lower EMBEDDING LR Further
items.spec: Set EMBEDDING_LR to 0.1, a much safer value for embedding layers compared to 0.6, preventing oscillations early in training.

items.title: Reduce Depth to Mini
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 4 to train a very small, fast model that might have higher signal-to-noise ratio and fit perfectly within the data budget, acting as a strong baseline.

items.title: Adjust Head Dimension
items.spec: Modify HEAD_DIM to 64 by adjusting how ASPECT_RATIO scales with depth or assuming a fixed dim_head, potentially improving attention efficiency for this specific vocabulary size.

items.title: Remove Weight Decay
items.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.0 to test if any regularization is needed for Muon, as the gradient-free updates might already regularize the model sufficiently.

items.title: Use Cosine Warmup

items.spec: Increase the DEPTH constant from 8 to 12. Since the training time is fixed, this will result in fewer training steps but may capture more complex patterns.

items.title: Increase Model Width
items.spec: Increase the ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 80. This increases the model dimension (model_dim = depth * ASPECT_RATIO) to improve representation capacity.

items.title: Decrease Head Dimension
items.spec: Decrease the HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64. This allows for more heads with the same total dimension, which can help with multi-head attention diversity.

items.title: Switch to Full Context
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SSSS'. This forces the model to attend to the full context rather than a sliding window, potentially improving long-range coherence.

items.title: Increase Weight Decay
items.spec: Increase WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.3. Higher weight decay can prevent the model from over-fitting on the limited data available in 300 seconds.

items.title: Reduce Weight Decay
items.spec: Decrease WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1. Lower weight decay might allow the model to learn more complex features if the training is under-fitting.

items.title: Increase Matrix LR
items.spec: Increase MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06. A slightly higher learning rate for the Muon optimizer might speed up convergence of the primary weights.

items.title: Decrease Matrix LR
items.spec: Decrease MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.03. A lower learning rate for the Muon optimizer might lead to more stable and precise weight updates.

items.title: Increase Embedding LR
items.spec: Increase EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.8. This allows the token embeddings to adapt more quickly during the training run.

items.title: Decrease Embedding LR
items.spec: Decrease EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.4. This stabilizes the embedding updates, which are often highly volatile in the early stages of training.

items.title: Increase Unembedding LR
items.spec: Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008. This helps the lm_head adapt faster to the representations learned by the backbone.

items.title: Decrease Unembedding LR
items.spec: Decrease UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.002. This keeps the output layer updates conservative to prevent gradient explosions.

items.title: Increase Scalar LR
items.spec: Increase SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.6. This speeds up the adaptation of layer-specific scalar parameters.

items.title: Decrease Scalar LR
items.spec: Decrease SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.4. This provides more stability for the scalar parameters, which can be sensitive to large updates.

items.title: Adjust Adam Betas
items.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.9, 0.99). These are the standard defaults and might provide more stable momentum than the current custom values.

items.title: Increase Warmup Ratio
items.spec: Increase WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.05. A small warmup phase can help stabilize the initial gradients of the Muon optimizer.

items.title: Decrease Warmdown Ratio
items.spec: Decrease WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.3. This spends more of the 300s budget on high-learning-rate training rather than decaying at the end.

items.title: Increase Final LR Fraction
items.spec: Increase FINAL_LR_FRAC from 0.0 to 0.1. This ensures the learning rate doesn't drop to zero, allowing the model to keep learning until the very last second.

items.title: Reduce Batch Size
items.spec: Decrease DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE from 64 to 32. This increases the number of weight updates per second (more noise, but faster iteration).

items.title: Increase Total Batch Size
items.spec: Increase TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20. This increases the global batch size, potentially smoothing the gradient and improving stability.

items.title: Modify Aspect Ratio to be Square
items.spec: Set ASPECT_RATIO to 1. This makes model_dim equal to depth, creating a very 'deep and narrow' architecture.

items.title: Very Deep/Narrow Architecture
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 16 and ASPECT_RATIO to 32. This is a variation of the deep-but-narrow approach to maximize layer count within VRAM limits.

items.title: Very Shallow/Wide Architecture
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 4 and ASPECT_RATIO to 128. This creates a 'shallow and wide' architecture to maximize width within VRAM limits.

items.title: Balanced Growth
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 12 and ASPECT_RATIO to 48. This is a more balanced growth strategy than the current 8/64 configuration.

items.title: Dropouts
items.spec: Introduce a 0.1 dropout rate in the attention layers by modifying the attention mechanism block (if applicable) or via a weight decay adjustment to simulate sparse updates.

items.title: Zero-Init Linear Layers
items.spec: Modify the model initialization to use zero-initialization for the weights of the attention layers (excluding the final layer) to improve stability in deep models.

items.title: Fast LR Decay
items.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.7. This forces a very aggressive learning rate decay, which can sometimes help the model 'settle' into a local minimum quickly.

items.title: No Warmdown
items.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.0. Keep the learning rate as high as possible for the entire duration of the 300 seconds.

items.title: Muon Stability
items.spec: Reduce MATRIX_LR to 0.01. Muon can be quite aggressive; a very low rate might allow for much smoother convergence in a short 300s window.

items.title: Max Model Width
items.spec: Increase ASPECT_RATIO to 128. This will make the model very wide, potentially capturing more features per layer, at the cost of depth.

items.title: SFQ-Attention,
items.spec: Increase total batch size by doubling DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 128 and increasing TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**20 to compensate for TF32 precision drop. Switch attention from standard to Soft Quantized Attention via a provided API that only uses FP32 in the pre-norm attention head while keeping weights to fit memory.

items.title: Check Your Float Scratchpads
items.spec: Rewrite the μMN training loop to use mixed precision for GEMMs but accumulate gradients in FP32 buffers before clipping and updating parameters, preventing precision errors in scaling factors.

items.title: Larger Optimizer State,
items.spec: Increase ASPECT_RATIO (model_dim) from 64 to 80 to increase embedding capacity, enabling the model to learn better token representations without changing the layer count or total batch size, leveraging the full 40GB capacity with stricter padding.

items.title: More Pure Tokens,
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.0 (currently 0.0), but ensure the linear AnnealingLR schedule starts at the final LR immediately and adjusts to adapt the momentum, reducing the risk of early divergence and data waste.

items.title: Head Scaling Momentum,
items.spec: Switch Matrix LR to an Adam-style optimizer for head dimensions (adding a small linear scaling factor multiplier) or use a decaying learning rate schedule instead of a constant learning rate to better match signal strength across layers.

items.title: Slightly Wider Attention,
items.spec: Reduce ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 56 or 48 to reduce memory footprint, allowing a larger effective batch size without increasing GPU pressure, potentially improving generalization by lowering parameter density.

items.title: Dynamic Context Length,
items.spec: Modify the sliding window pattern from 'SSSL' to 'SSSS' or 'LLLL' to test if reducing or expanding context window size per token step improves training stability and convergence speed under the given constraints.

items.title: Higher Precision Scaling,
items.spec: Use FP16 for forward passes and FP32 for backward passes (standard practice) while ensuring the micro-batch accumulation uses FP64 for stability in the scaling factors, which can improve convergence speed.

items.title: Reduce Over-parameterization,
items.spec: Halve ASPECT_RATIO to 32 to significantly reduce GPU memory usage, allowing the use of a larger true batch size to increase gradient signal quality without modifying other hyperparameters.

items.title: Accelerate Learning from Preset Autotuned Hyperparameters,
items.spec: Instead of manually tuning, use postal scale optimization to automatically find the optimal balance of learning rates and gradients, replacing the current manual setup with a more adaptive strategy.

Increase Matrix VRAM Efficiency
title
items.spec: Increase DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 80 (e.g., using mixed precision or sparse attention) to maximize VRAM utilization without out-of-memory crashes, improving training speed by processing more batches per step.

items.title: Reduce Attention Head Width
items.spec: Decrease HEAD_DIM from 128 to 96 or lower to reduce the memory footprint per layer, potentially allowing a larger total batch size without changing GPU architecture or batch size constraints.

items.title: Adjust Learning Rate for Embeddings
items.spec: Increase EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.8 for faster convergence of token representations, especially in early training, improving the model's ability to encode diverse semantic information within the fixed time budget.

items.title: Reduce Warm-down Period
items.spec: Decrease WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.2 to allow the learning rate to remain higher for longer, promoting faster convergence within the fixed 300-second window.

items.title: Increase Weight Decay
items.spec: Increase WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.4 or 0.5 to reduce overfitting and improve generalization, especially beneficial when the model is small and prone to fitting the training data too closely.

items.title: Decrease Learning Rates Uniformly
items.spec: Reduce all learning rates by a factor of 1.2 (e.g., MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.033) to stabilize training and avoid overshooting optimal weights, which can lead to smoother convergence.

items.title: Adjust Sliding Window Pattern
items.spec: Modify WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'LLLL' to test the effect of longer context windows during training, which can improve the model's ability to handle long-range dependencies.

items.title: Use Exponential Decay for Learning Rate
items.spec: Replace the linear warmup/windown schedule with an exponential decay schedule to gradually reduce the learning rate, which can help the model converge more smoothly and avoid oscillations near the end of training.

items.title: Increase Embedding Timestep
items.spec: Modify the embedding layer timestep to match the layer timestep more closely, ensuring more consistent gradients across different parts of the network and improving overall stability.

items.title: Use Different Batch Norm
items.spec: If applicable, replace standard LayerNorm with RMSNorm or similar normalization techniques to improve training stability and reduce the risk of exploding gradients in deep layers.

items.title: Leverage Data Augmentation
items.spec: Introduce simple data augmentation techniques such as token dropping or noise injection to increase the robustness of the training data and improve the model's generalization capabilities.

items.title: Fine-tune MoU Later
items.spec: Post-train the model using a smaller learning rate for fine-tuning on a different dataset or task to improve its final performance and generalization without affecting the original training process.

items.title: Use Gradient Clipping
items.spec: Add global gradient clipping to limit the maximum norm of gradients, preventing gradient explosion and ensuring more stable updates during training.

items.title: Adjust Attention Heads
items.spec: Modify the number of attention heads or their dimensions to better suit the task's complexity, potentially improving the model's ability to capture complex patterns in the training data.

items.title: Use Different Optimizer
items.spec: Experiment with switching from Muon (adaptively scaled gradients) to a standard AdamW optimizer to see if a more traditional approach yields better results given the limited training time.

items.title: Apply Curriculum Learning
items.spec: Implement a curriculum learning strategy where the model is first trained on easier samples and gradually exposed to harder ones, which can speed up convergence and improve final performance.

items.title: Reduce Depth for Efficiency
items.spec: Reduce DEPTH from 8 to 6 or fewer layers to reduce computational load and allow for a larger effective batch size, potentially improving generalization by focusing resources on fewer but more robust layers.

items.title: Use Residual Dropout
items.spec: Add a small amount of dropout to residual connections to regularize the model and prevent overfitting, especially beneficial when the model is small and prone to learning noise in the training data.

items.title: Increase Learning Rate for LM Head
items.spec: Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR to allow the output layer to adapt more quickly, potentially improving the model's ability to generate accurate predictions early in training.

items.title: Use Cosine Annealing for LR
items.spec: Replace linear annealing with cosine annealing for the learning rate schedule, which provides a smoother decay profile and can help the model converge more reliably.

items.title: Increase Depth, Decrease Width
items.spec: Decrease ASPECT_RATIO to 32 and increase DEPTH to 16. This maintains a similar total parameter count but increases the depth of the transformation, which often helps with modeling complex dependencies in small models.

items.title: Increase Depth, Decrease Width (Alternative)
items.spec: Decrease ASPECT_RATIO to 16 and increase DEPTH to 32. This is an even more extreme version of the depth-first approach to see if the model can benefit from deeper serial processing.

items.title: Optimize Head Dimension
items.spec: Change HEAD_DIM from 128 to 96. Smaller head dimensions can sometimes lead to better generalization in very small models by forcing more compact representations.

items.title: Optimize Head Dimension (Alternative)
items.spec: Change HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64. This significantly reduces the width of the attention heads, potentially allowing for more heads or more compact information processing.

items.title: Full Context Window
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN to 'LLLL'. Moving from a sliding window to a full context window allows the model to attend to all tokens simultaneously, which may improve long-range coherence.

items.title: Reduce Weight Decay
items.spec: Lower WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1. High weight decay can sometimes overly constrain the capacity of very small models that need to memorize basic patterns.

items.title: Increase Weight Decay
items.spec: Increase WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.4. More aggressive weight decay might help prevent overfitting on a small parameter budget by forcing more sparse-like activations.

items.title: Linear LR Warmup
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.1. Adding a short warmup period can help stabilize the initial gradient updates, especially when using Muon.

items.title: Extended LR Warmup
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.2. A longer warmup period provides more time for the Adam and Muon optimizers to settle before the high-learning-rate phase.

items.title: Extended LR Warmdown
items.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.7. A longer warmdown period allows the model to perform a final 'fine-tuning' phase at very low learning rates.

items.title: Increase Matrix LR
items.spec: Increase MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06. Since Muon handles the bulk of the parameters, a slightly higher learning rate might accelerate convergence within the 300s window.

items.title: Decrease Matrix LR
items.spec: Decrease MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.02. A slower learning rate for the matrix parameters might lead to more stable convergence and lower final loss.

items.title: Increase Scalar LR
items.spec: Increase SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.7. This allows the per-layer scalars to adapt more quickly to the training data.

items.title: Decrease Scalar LR
items.spec: Decrease SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.3. Slower updates for scalars can prevent 'explosive' shifts in layer normalization/scaling early in training.

items.title: Adjust Adam Betas
items.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS to (0.9, 0.999). Using standard Adam betas might be more stable than the current (0.8, 0.95) for this specific task.

items.title: Aggressive Matrix LR
items.spec: Increase MATRIX_LR to 0.1. This is a high-risk, high-reward attempt to maximize progress in the short 300s window.

items.title: Increase Device Batch Size
items.spec: Increase DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 80. If it doesn't OOM, a larger effective batch size might provide more stable gradient estimates.

items.title: Decrease Device Batch Size
items.spec: Decrease DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 48. A smaller batch size increases the number of weight updates performed within the 300s wall-clock time.

items.title: Decrease Total Batch Size
items.spec: Decrease TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18. This slightly lowers the gradient noise but might allow for a more stable path toward the optimum.

items.title: Increase Total Batch Size
items.spec: Increase TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**20. A larger batch size might improve the quality of each individual gradient step.

items.title: Unembedding LR Adjustment
items.spec: Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.01. This speeds up the learning of the output head, which is often a bottleneck in small models.

items.title: Embedding LR Adjustment
items.spec: Increase EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.8. Faster learning for the embeddings might help the model map tokens to concepts more quickly.

items.title: Zero Final LR Fraction
items.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1. This ensures the learning rate doesn't drop to zero too quickly, maintaining some ability to learn at the end of the run.

items.title: High Aspect Ratio
items.spec: Increase ASPECT_RATIO to 128 and decrease DEPTH to 4. This makes the model very 'wide' and 'shallow', testing if high-dimensional width is superior for this task.

items.title: Extreme Depth
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 16 and ASPECT_RATIO to 32. This is the most 'deep' configuration feasible under the parameter budget.

items.title: Mixed Weight Decay
items.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.15. A middle ground between the current 0.2 and a more conservative 0.1.

items.title: Aggressive Warmdown
items.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.9. A very long tail at the end of the 300s might allow for precise convergence.

items.title: Tiny Batch
items.spec: Set DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32. This maximizes the number of optimizer steps per second at the cost of potentially noisier gradients.

items.title: Muon Learning Rate Boost
items.spec: Increase MATRIX_LR to 0.08. Push the Muon optimizer harder to see if the model can catch up to the baseline in 300s.

items.title: Wide and Deep Balance
items.spec: Set ASPECT_RATIO to 48 and DEPTH to 10. A balanced approach to finding the sweet spot between width and depth.

items.title: Muon momentum warmup
items.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Only the Muon momentum value changes; the Nesterov flag, LR and weight decay stay as they are.

items.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations
items.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside the Muon update from the current count to 3. This cuts optimizer overhead per step, so more steps fit in the 300 s budget. Keep the coefficient set unchanged.

items.title: No weight decay on embeddings and scalars
items.spec: Apply WEIGHT_DECAY only to the Muon matrix parameters. Set weight decay to 0 for the token embedding, the lm_head, and all per-layer scalar parameters. Keep all learning rates unchanged.

items.title: Shape-aware Muon LR scaling
items.spec: Scale each matrix parameter's Muon update by sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) so that tall and wide matrices receive comparable effective step sizes. Keep MATRIX_LR as the base value and do not change the other optimizer groups.

items.title: Adam beta1 lower for scalars
items.spec: Change the beta1 of the Adam optimizer used for scalar parameters to 0.9 and leave beta2 at 0.95. Apply this only to the scalar parameter group; embeddings and lm_head keep ADAM_BETAS as currently defined.

items.title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear
items.spec: Replace the linear learning-rate warmdown with a cosine decay that starts at the point where WARMDOWN_RATIO begins and reaches FINAL_LR_FRAC at the end of the time budget. Apply the same multiplier to all parameter groups.

items.title: Longer warmdown
items.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the learning rate decays over the last 70% of the time budget. Leave all other schedule settings and hyperparameters unchanged.

items.title: Short warmup for stability
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so each parameter group ramps its learning rate linearly from zero over the first 2% of the time budget before the warmdown begins. Keep the rest of the schedule unchanged.

items.title: Batch-size ramp
items.spec: Start with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE at 2**17 tokens and double it at fixed time fractions (for example at 25% and 50% of the budget) until it reaches 2**19. Implement this by adjusting gradient accumulation steps, keeping DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE fixed, and scale the learning rates with the square root of the batch ratio.

items.title: Smaller total batch size
items.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 so each optimizer step uses about 262K tokens. This gives roughly twice as many optimizer steps in the fixed time budget. Keep all learning rates unchanged.

items.title: Logit soft-capping
items.spec: Apply a soft cap to the output logits before the cross-entropy loss, using logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15). The cap is applied in the forward pass during both training and evaluation of the model's own output, and nothing else changes.

items.title: QK-norm with per-head learnable gain
items.spec: Normalize queries and keys with RMSNorm before the attention dot product, and multiply each head's query by a learnable scalar initialized to 1. This stabilizes attention logits at high learning rates.

items.title: Skip connection from the input embedding
items.spec: Store the normalized token embedding x0 after the embedding layer. At the start of each transformer block, add x0 scaled by a learnable per-layer scalar initialized to 0. This gives every layer direct access to the input token representation.

items.title: SwiGLU MLP at matched parameters
items.spec: Replace the MLP with a SwiGLU block whose hidden width is set to 8/3 times model_dim, rounded to a multiple of 64, so that the parameter count stays close to the current MLP. Keep the rest of the block unchanged.

items.title: Parallel attention and MLP blocks
items.spec: Change each transformer block to compute attention and the MLP from the same normalized input and sum both outputs into the residual stream, in the GPT-J style, instead of applying them sequentially. Keep the number of layers and widths unchanged.

items.title: Zero-initialized residual projections
items.spec: Initialize the output projection of each attention block and each MLP block to zero, so every residual branch starts as the identity. Keep the default initialization for all other weights.

items.title: Rotary base increase
items.spec: Change the RoPE base frequency from 10000 to 100000. This gives the attention heads longer-wavelength position signals within the sliding-window context. Nothing else changes.

items.title: Alternating window pattern
items.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN to "SL" so that the full-context and half-context attention layers alternate. This changes the mix of long and short attention relative to the current "SSSL" pattern.

items.title: Shallower and wider model
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 6 and ASPECT_RATIO to 96 so model_dim becomes 576, and set HEAD_DIM to 96 so that the model keeps 6 heads. Keep all other hyperparameters unchanged.

items.title: Deeper and narrower model
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO to 48 so model_dim becomes 480, and set HEAD_DIM to 96 so that the model keeps 5 heads. Keep all other hyperparameters unchanged.

items.title: Learnable per-head attention temperature
items.spec: Add one learnable scalar per attention head that multiplies the attention logits, initialized so that the scale matches the default 1/sqrt(head_dim). Keep it in the scalar parameter group with the current scalar learning rate.

items.title: Untied embeddings with separate initialization
items.spec: Keep the token embedding and lm_head as separate weights, and initialize the lm_head with a small standard deviation of 0.001 while leaving the embedding init unchanged. This is a change to initialization only.

items.title: Weight decay ramp-down
items.spec: Linearly decay WEIGHT_DECAY from its current value to 0 over the course of the time budget, so the regularization is strongest early and absent in the final phase. Apply this to the Muon group only.

items.title: Stronger weight decay
items.spec: Raise the Muon WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.4 and keep the same decay schedule. This tests whether a stronger constraint on the matrix weights helps in the short training regime.

items.title: Weight EMA for the final model
items.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of all model parameters with decay 0.999, updated after each optimizer step. Use the EMA weights as the trained model when the harness calls evaluation, and leave the evaluation call itself unchanged.

items.title: Compile the optimizer step
items.spec: Wrap the Muon and Adam parameter update functions in torch.compile so the update kernels are fused. This should increase steps per second without changing the optimizer math.

items.title: Shorter sequence with larger micro-batch
items.spec: If train.py defines a sequence length constant, halve it and double DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE so that tokens per micro-step stay constant. This tests whether more sequences per batch helps the optimizer under the same throughput budget. If memory would exceed 40 GB, reduce to 96.

items.title: Curriculum with shorter attention window early
items.spec: For the first 20% of the time budget, force all attention layers to use the short sliding window. After that, switch back to the WINDOW_PATTERN layout. This is a schedule over the attention window and does not change the parameter count.

items.title: Lower embedding learning rate
items.spec: Reduce EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3 while keeping the other learning rates unchanged. This tests whether the current high embedding step size is causing noisy token representations.

items.title: Muon momentum warmup
items.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold it at 0.95. Leave Nesterov on and change nothing else in the Muon update.

items.title: No weight decay on embeddings and lm_head
items.spec: Set weight decay to 0 for the Adam-optimized token embedding and lm_head parameter groups, keeping WEIGHT_DECAY only for the Muon matrix params. Implement by giving those Adam param groups weight_decay=0.0.

items.title: Lower embedding LR sweep
items.spec: Reduce EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3 and leave all other learning rates unchanged. This tests whether the high embedding learning rate is overshooting in the short 300 s budget.

items.title: Lower scalar LR sweep
items.spec: Reduce SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.25, keeping the other LRs unchanged. This tests whether the per-layer scalar gains (residual and x0 mixing) are too aggressive.

items.title: Adam beta1 0.9 with beta2 0.99
items.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.9, 0.99) for all Adam-optimized groups (embedding, lm_head, scalars). Muon betas are unaffected.

items.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations for Muon
items.spec: Reduce the Newton-Schulz orthogonalization steps in Muon from 5 to 3. This makes each optimizer step cheaper so more steps fit in 300 s, at a small cost in update accuracy.

items.title: Shape-aware Muon update scaling
items.spec: Scale the orthogonalized Muon update per matrix by 0.2 * sqrt(max(rows, cols)) so its RMS roughly matches AdamW. Then use a shared LR near the Adam scale. Keep the existing sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) factor removed so only this scale applies.

items.title: Longer warmdown
items.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the LR decays over the final 70% of the time budget. Keep WARMUP_RATIO at 0.0 and FINAL_LR_FRAC at 0.0.

items.title: Short linear warmup
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.03 so the LR ramps linearly from 0 over the first 3% of the time budget before the warmdown begins. This guards against early instability from the high Muon and embedding LRs.

items.title: Cosine warmdown shape
items.spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine decay from the peak LR to FINAL_LR_FRAC over the WARMDOWN_RATIO portion of the time budget. Keep the same ratio and endpoints.

items.title: Non-zero final LR fraction
items.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 so the LR decays to 10% of its peak instead of zero. This keeps some learning signal at the end of the run.

items.title: Smaller total batch size
items.spec: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 tokens per optimizer step. Keep the LRs unchanged. More optimizer steps fit into the fixed 300 s window.

items.title: Batch size ramp
items.spec: Start with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE at 2**17 and double it at fixed time fractions (for example at 25% and 60% of the budget) until it reaches 2**19. Keep gradient accumulation consistent with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 and recompute the accumulation steps at each change.

items.title: Scale matrix LR with batch size
items.spec: After setting TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18, multiply MATRIX_LR by sqrt(0.5), about 0.028, to compensate for the smaller batch. Leave the other LRs unchanged.

items.title: Narrower model width
items.spec: Set ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 48 so model_dim is 384 at DEPTH 8, keeping HEAD_DIM 128 and the rest unchanged. This trades width for faster steps.

items.title: Smaller attention head dimension
items.spec: Set HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64, which doubles the number of attention heads at the same model_dim. Keep all other hyperparameters the same.

items.title: Alternating sliding window pattern
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "SL" so every second layer uses full context and the others use half context. This tests whether more full-attention layers help at this small depth.

items.title: Value residual from first layer
items.spec: Add a learned scalar per layer that mixes the first layer's attention value vectors into each later layer's values (ResFormer style). Initialize the scalars to 0 so the model starts unchanged. Only the value path changes.

items.title: Logit soft-capping
items.spec: Apply logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15) to the lm_head output before the cross-entropy loss. This bounds extreme logits and can stabilize the high-LR Muon training.

items.title: Learnable per-head QK gain
items.spec: After QK-norm, multiply each head's query and key by a learnable per-head scalar gain initialized to 1.0 (or sqrt(head_dim) equivalent). Keep the gains in the scalar Adam group.

items.title: Narrower MLP expansion
items.spec: Change the MLP hidden width from 4x model_dim to 3x model_dim. This saves parameters and compute per step so more training steps fit in 300 s.

items.title: Deeper and narrower model
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO to 48, giving model_dim about 480 rounded up to a multiple of HEAD_DIM 128. Keep WINDOW_PATTERN and the rest unchanged. Watch the step rate to confirm it still fits the time budget.

items.title: Residual-scaled initialization
items.spec: Zero-initialize the output projections of attention and MLP blocks, and scale the other residual-branch init by 1/sqrt(2 * DEPTH). This keeps the residual stream variance stable at the start of training.

items.title: Z-loss on logits
items.spec: Add 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) to the training loss to keep the logit normalizer near zero. Apply it to training only, and leave the evaluation path unchanged.

items.title: Gradient norm clipping
items.spec: Clip the global gradient norm to 1.0 before each optimizer step. This guards against occasional loss spikes at the high peak LRs.

items.title: Weight decay sweep for Muon
items.spec: Change WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1 for the Muon matrix params and keep the other settings unchanged. This tests whether the current decay is too strong for the short run.

items.title: Weight decay ramp down
items.spec: Scale the Muon weight decay linearly from its full value to 0 across the warmdown period so the model settles without decay pulling weights in at the end. Keep the decay unchanged during the stable phase.

items.title: Sequence length curriculum
items.spec: Train with a shorter effective sequence length (for example 512 tokens, by splitting each batch into more, shorter sequences with the same token count) for the first 40% of the time budget, then switch to the full context length. Keep the total tokens per step unchanged.

items.title: Weight EMA for final model
items.spec: Keep an exponential moving average of the model weights with decay 0.999, updated after each optimizer step. Use the EMA weights as the model that gets evaluated at the end of training. Do not change the evaluation call itself.

items.title: Fused optimizer step for throughput
items.spec: Use fused AdamW for the Adam-optimized groups (fused=True where supported) and batch the Muon parameter updates by shape. This increases steps per second without changing the optimizer math.

items.title: DeepNorm Architecture
items.spec: Implement DeepNorm by replacing standard LayerNorm with a modified version that scales weights based on the norm of the input, helping stabilize training in deeper models.

items.title: Root Mean Square LayerNorm
items.spec: Replace standard LayerNorm with RMSNorm to reduce the computational overhead and potentially stabilize the training of the transformer blocks.

items.title: Rotary Positional Embeddings (RoPE)
items.spec: Replace standard absolute positional embeddings (if used) or inject RoPE into the attention mechanism to improve positional generalization.

items.title: SwiGLU Activation
items.spec: Replace the standard ReLU or GELU activations in the Feed Forward Network with SwiGLU for better non-linear representation learning.

items.title: Grouped Query Attention (GQA)
items.spec: Implement GQA by splitting the number of query heads while keeping the number of key/value heads smaller to reduce memory bandwidth during training.

items.title: FlashAttention-2 Integration
items.spec: Replace the standard attention computation with a manual implementation of the FlashAttention-2 tiling logic to speed up training and reduce memory usage.

items.title: Weight Tie Embeddings
items.spec: Tie the weights of the input embedding layer and the output lm_head to reduce the number of parameters and force shared representations.

items.title: Stochastic Depth
items.spec: Implement Stochastic Depth by randomly dropping layers during training (with a linear decay schedule) to improve generalization.

items.title: DropPath
items.spec: Implement DropPath (similar to Stochastic Depth but applied to residual connections) to improve the robustness of the residual blocks.

items.title: Label Smoothing
items.spec: Apply a small amount of label smoothing (e.g., 0.1) to the cross-entropy loss to prevent the model from becoming overconfident.

items.title: Weight Decay for Adam
items.spec: Ensure that weight decay is applied correctly to the Adam optimizer parameters (matrix_lr parameters) rather than just the gradient penalty.

items.title: AdamW Optimizer
items.spec: Replace the custom Muon/Adam mix with a pure AdamW implementation for the matrix parameters to see if standard weight decay behaves better.

items.title: Lookahead Optimizer
items.spec: Wrap the existing optimizer in a Lookahead mechanism to stabilize the trajectory of the weights and improve final convergence.

items.title: Learning Rate Warmup
items.spec: Implement a linear warmup for the first 5% of the training steps to prevent early gradient explosion.

items.title: Cosine Annealing
items.spec: Replace the current scheduler with a Cosine Annealing schedule to provide a smoother decay of the learning rate towards the end of the 300s.

items.title: OneCycleLR
items.spec: Implement the OneCycleLR policy to reach a high learning rate quickly and then decay, which can often lead to faster convergence in short runs.

items.title: Linear Learning Rate Decay
items.spec: Change the current warmdown to a linear decay that starts earlier to ensure the model settles into a local minimum before the 300s limit.

items.title: Gradient Clipping
items.spec: Implement global gradient clipping (e.g., max_norm=1.0) to prevent huge gradients from destabilizing the model during high-LR phases.

items.title: Mixed Precision (FP16/BF16)
items.spec: Use `torch.cuda.amp.autocast` and `GradScaler` to train in mixed precision, potentially allowing for a larger batch size or faster iterations.

items.title: Increase Depth, Decrease Width
items.spec: Modify ASPECT_RATIO and DEPTH to increase total depth while decreasing width (keeping total params similar) to improve logic.

items.title: Decrease Depth, Increase Width
items.spec: Modify ASPECT_RATIO and DEPTH to decrease depth and increase width to prioritize 'breadth' of knowledge over sequential reasoning.

items.title: Increase Batch Size to 128
items.spec: Attempt to squeeze a batch size of 128 into the 40GB VRAM by using gradient checkpointing or a smaller model width.

items.title: Gradient Checkpointing
items.spec: Enable `torch.utils.checkpoint` on the transformer blocks to trade computation for memory, allowing for a larger batch size or model.

items.title: Sequence Length Scaling
items.spec: Adjust the input sequence length (if adjustable in the loop) to find the optimal balance between per-token information and total throughput.

items.title: $	ext{1/x}$ Learning Rate Scaling
items.spec: Scale the learning rates (EMBEDDING_LR, etc.) by a factor proportional to the batch size to maintain consistent gradient scales.

items.title: $	ext{1/x}$ Weight Decay Scaling
items.spec: Scale the WEIGHT_DECAY parameter relative to the batch size to maintain regularization strength.

items.title: Pre-LayerNorm vs Post-LayerNorm
items.spec: If the model is Post-LN, switch to Pre-LN (norm before the sublayer) to improve training stability at higher learning rates.

items.title: Head Dimension Tuning
items.spec: Change HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 or 256 to see how it affects the attention mechanism's expressive power and memory.

items.title: Optimizer Parameter Separation
items.spec: Separate the learning rates for different layers more granularly (e.g., different LRs for the first and last 25% of layers).

items.title: Weight Initialization Tuning
items.spec: Replace the default Xavier/Kaiming init with a custom normal distribution or a different scaling factor to improve early training stability.

items.title: Increase Depth
items.spec: Increase DEPTH from 8 to 10. This aims to increase the model's capacity to learn complex patterns within the same total parameter budget by rearranging the depth-to-width ratio.

items.title: Increase Aspect Ratio
items.spec: Increase ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 80. This makes the model wider relative to its depth, which often helps with learning broader feature representations at the cost of more parameters.

items.title: Decrease Aspect Ratio
items.spec: Decrease ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 48. This makes the model deeper relative to its width, which can sometimes improve performance on tasks requiring sequential reasoning.

items.title: Increase Head Dimension
items.spec: Increase HEAD_DIM from 128 to 160. Larger head dimensions can provide higher-dimensional spaces for attention, potentially capturing more nuanced relationships.

items.title: Decrease Head Dimension
items.spec: Decrease HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64. Reducing head dimension can save memory and parameters, potentially allowing for more heads or more depth.

items.title: Increase Matrix LR
items.spec: Increase MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06. A slightly higher learning rate for Muon-optimized weights might accelerate convergence in the limited 300s window.

items.title: Decrease Matrix LR
items.spec: Decrease MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.03. A lower learning rate might stabilize training and prevent divergence in the short 300s timeframe.

items.title: Increase Scalar LR
items.spec: Increase SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.7. This allows the Adam-optimized scalar parameters (like LayerNorm gains) to adapt more quickly during the training run.

items.title: Decrease Scalar LR
items.spec: Decrease SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.3. A lower rate for scalars can prevent aggressive changes to normalization layers early in training.

items.title: Increase Weight Decay
items.spec: Increase WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.3. Stronger regularization can help prevent overfitting in a small model with limited training time.

items.title: Decrease Weight Decay
items.spec: Decrease WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1. Reducing weight decay might allow the model to fit the training data more closely in a short timeframe.

items.title: Increase Warmdown Ratio
items.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7. Spending more time in the warmdown phase can help the model settle into a stable local minimum.

items.title: Decrease Warmdown Ratio
items.spec: Decrease WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.3. This leaves more time for the high-LR learning phase, potentially leading to more significant weight updates.

items.title: Increase Final LR Fraction
items.spec: Increase FINAL_LR_FRAC from 0.0 to 0.1. Ensuring the learning rate doesn't drop to zero might help with final convergence in very short runs.

items.title: Increase Warmup Ratio
items.spec: Increase WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.1. A short warmup can prevent early divergence and help stabilize the initial gradients.

items.title: Increase Embedding LR
items.spec: Increase EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.7. Higher learning rates for embeddings can help the model learn token representations faster.

items.title: Decrease Embedding LR
items.spec: Decrease EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.5. Lowering the embedding LR might stabilize the model if it starts to overfit the vocabulary quickly.

items.title: Increase Unembedding LR
items.spec: Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008. Faster adaptation of the lm_head might improve the final val_bpb.

items.title: Decrease Unembedding LR
items.spec: Decrease UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.002. Slower updates to the lm_head can sometimes lead to better generalization.

items.title: Shift Adam Betas
items.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.9, 0.99). Using standard Adam betas might provide more stable momentum for the scalar and embedding parameters.

items.title: Large Batch Gradient Accumulation
items.spec: Maintain DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at 64 but simulate a larger effective batch size by increasing the number of gradient accumulation steps (if the loop allows) or by adjusting TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE logic.

items.title: Mini Batch Optimization
items.spec: Reduce DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE from 64 to 32. This increases the number of updates per second, which might be beneficial in a 300s wall-clock constraint.

items.title: Change Window Pattern
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SSSS'. This changes the sliding window configuration to a different structural distribution.

items.title: Change Window Pattern 2
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'LLLL'. This forces a different sliding window context length distribution.

items.title: Aggressive Weight Decay
items.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.5. A very high weight decay can act as a strong prior towards simpler, more generalizable solutions.

items.title: Zero Weight Decay
items.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.0. Removing weight decay entirely might allow the model to capture more specific nuances in the 300s window.

items.title: Increase LR Scaling
items.spec: Scale all LR values (MATRIX_LR, SCALAR_LR, etc.) by 1.2. This increases the overall speed of learning at the risk of instability.

items.title: Decrease LR Scaling
items.spec: Scale all LR values by 0.8. This slows down training but might lead to a higher quality local minimum.

items.title: Deep and Narrow
items.spec: Increase DEPTH to 12 and decrease ASPECT_RATIO to 48. This creates a much deeper, narrower model to see if sequential depth is preferred.

items.title: Wide and Shallow
items.spec: Decrease DEPTH to 4 and increase ASPECT_RATIO to 128. This creates a very wide, shallow model to see if parallelism is preferred.

items.title: Fast Convergence Schedule
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.0 and WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.1. This maximizes the time spent in the high-learning-rate region of the schedule.

items.title: Increase Depth
items.spec: Increase DEPTH from 8 to 12. Since the budget is wall-clock time, this might slow down the total number of steps but could improve capacity and lower val_bpb.

items.title: Increase Aspect Ratio
items.spec: Increase ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 128. This increases the model dimension, providing more capacity per layer.

items.title: Reduce Head Dim
items.spec: Decrease HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64. This allows for more heads or more efficient attention patterns.

items.title: Weight Decay Adjustment
items.spec: Decrease WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1. A lower weight decay might prevent excessive shrinkage of weights in a small model.

items.title: Increase Matrix LR
items.spec: Increase MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06 to speed up convergence of the heavy weights.

items.title: Increase Scalar LR
items.spec: Increase SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.7. If scalar components are important, a higher LR may help them adapt faster.

items.title: Reduce Embedding LR
items.spec: Decrease EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.4 to prevent catastrophic forgetting of token identities.

items.title: Warmup Period
items.spec: Change WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.05 to stabilize the initial training phase.

items.title: Warmdown Adjustment
items.spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.3 to allow for more training time at the peak learning rate.

items.title: Final LR Fraction
items.spec: Change FINAL_LR_FRAC from 0.0 to 0.1 to avoid a sharp drop-off at the very end of the 300s window.

items.title: Increase Batch Size
items.spec: Increase DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE from 64 to 72 (if memory allows) to increase the effective global batch size.

items.title: Decrease Batch Size
items.spec: Decrease DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE from 64 to 48 to get more updates per second, even if the per-step gradient is noisier.

items.title: Change Window Pattern
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SSSS' to change the spatial/contextual focus of the sliding window.

items.title: Adam Beta1 Tuning
items.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.9, 0.999) for standard Adam momentum behavior.

items.title: Muon Weight Decay
items.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.0 to see if the Muon optimizer performs better without explicit decay on the matrix weights.

items.title: Unembedding LR Tuning
items.spec: Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.01 to speed up the mapping from hidden states back to vocabulary.

items.title: Narrow/Deep Tradeoff
items.spec: Decrease ASPECT_RATIO to 32 and increase DEPTH to 16 to create a 'deeper' model with smaller hidden layers.

items.title: Wide/Shallow Tradeoff
items.spec: Increase ASPECT_RATIO to 128 and decrease DEPTH to 4 to create a 'wider' model with fewer layers.

items.title: Aggressive Warmdown
items.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.8 to perform a very slow annealing of the learning rate.

items.title: Large Matrix LR
items.spec: Set MATRIX_LR to 0.1 to aggressively train the weight matrices.

items.title: Small Matrix LR
items.spec: Set MATRIX_LR to 0.02 to ensure stability in the weight matrix updates.

items.title: Weight Decay Increase
items.spec: Increase WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.3 to encourage more sparse/regularized weight distributions.

items.title: No Warmup
items.spec: Ensure WARMUP_RATIO remains 0.0 but increase the initial learning rate of the Matrix LR.

items.title: High Unembedding LR
items.spec: Set UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.05 to prioritize the final layer's training.

items.title: Head Dim Reduction
items.spec: Set HEAD_DIM to 64 and increase the number of heads (implied by dimension logic) to improve multi-head representation.

items.title: Batch Size Smoothing
items.spec: Decrease DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 to maximize the number of steps completed in 300s.

items.title: Low Weight Decay
items.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.05 to find a middle ground between 0.2 and 0.0.

items.title: Scalar LR Reduction
items.spec: Decrease SCALAR_LR to 0.3 to slow down the adaptation of per-layer scalars.

items.title: Embedding LR Increase
items.spec: Increase EMBEDDING_LR to 0.8 to force faster adaptation of the token embeddings.

items.title: Extreme Depth
items.spec: Increase DEPTH to 16 while keeping ASPECT_RATIO at 64, pushing the limits of the 300s budget.

items.title: Increase Depth
items.spec: Increase DEPTH from 8 to 12. Increasing depth often provides better scaling for representation learning within the same total parameter budget.

items.title: Increase Aspect Ratio
items.spec: Increase ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 128. This makes the model wider, allowing for more parallel capacity in the matrix multiplications.

items.title: Reduce Aspect Ratio
items.spec: Decrease ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 48. This makes the model deeper/narrower, which can sometimes improve generalization in small models.

items.title: Reduce Head Dimension
items.spec: Decrease HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64. Reducing the head dimension can improve the number of attention heads or reduce memory pressure.

items.title: Increase Head Dimension
items.spec: Increase HEAD_DIM from 128 to 256. Larger head dimensions can capture more complex relationships but may increase the risk of overfitting.

items.title: RMSNorm Initialization
items.spec: Modify the weight initialization of the LayerNorm/RMSNorm layers to be slightly more conservative (smaller variance) to stabilize early training.

items.title: Switch to RoPE
items.spec: Replace standard positional embeddings (if any) with Rotary Positional Embeddings (RoPE) to improve long-range dependency modeling.

items.title: Weight Decay Scaling
items.spec: Increase WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.3. Stronger regularization can help prevent the model from memorizing the small training set.

items.title: Reduce Weight Decay
items.spec: Decrease WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.1. If the model is underfitting, reducing weight decay might allow it to capture more nuances of the data.

items.title: Stochastic Depth
items.spec: Implement Stochastic Depth (DropPath) during training, randomly dropping entire transformer layers with a small probability.

items.title: Dropout Layer
items.spec: Add a standard Dropout layer (p=0.1) after the attention and MLP blocks to improve generalization.

items.title: Label Smoothing
items.spec: Implement label smoothing (e.g., 0.1) in the final loss calculation to prevent the model from becoming overconfident in its predictions.

items.title: Increase Matrix LR
items.spec: Increase MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06. Since Muon is used for matrix parameters, a higher learning rate might accelerate convergence.

items.title: Decrease Matrix LR
items.spec: Decrease MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.02. A more conservative learning rate for the main weights can prevent divergence.

items.title: Increase Scalar LR
items.spec: Increase SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.8. This allows the per-layer scalars to adapt faster to the data distribution.

items.title: Decrease Scalar LR
items.spec: Decrease SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.3. Slower adaptation of scalars can provide more stability in the training dynamics.

items.title: Embedding LR Tuning
items.spec: Increase EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.8. Give the model more freedom to learn the initial token representations.

items.title: Unembedding LR Tuning
items.spec: Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.01. A larger learning rate for the head can help it align more quickly with the internal representations.

items.title: Adam Betas
items.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS to (0.9, 0.999), the standard defaults, to see if the custom (0.8, 0.95) is hindering performance.

items.title: Warmup Fraction
items.spec: Increase WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.1. A small amount of warmup can prevent the gradients from exploding in the first few steps.

items.title: Warmdown Fraction
items.spec: Increase WARDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7. A longer cooldown period can help the model settle into a better local minimum.

items.title: Final LR Fraction
items.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1. This will ensure the model doesn't stop at a perfectly zeroed learning rate, but rather a very small one.

items.title: Cosine Decay Schedule
items.spec: Ensure the learning rate follows a cosine decay schedule over the 300s window (if not already the default behavior).

items.title: Increase Device Batch Size
items.spec: Increase DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 96 (if it fits in 40GB). Larger batch sizes provide more stable gradient estimates.

items.title: Decrease Device Batch Size
items.spec: Decrease DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 48. Smaller batch sizes introduce more noise, which can act as a regularizer.

items.title: Gradient Clipping
items.spec: Implement global gradient clipping with a max norm of 1.0 to prevent large updates from destabilizing the training.

items.title: Mixed Precision Training
items.spec: Ensure the training uses FP16 or BF16 mixed precision to increase throughput and potentially improve training dynamics.

items.title: Weight Initialization
items.spec: Change the standard deviation of the weight initialization from 0.02 to 0.01 for all linear layers.

items.title: Layer Scaling
items.spec: Add a scaling factor (e.g., 1/sqrt(d_model)) to the attention output before the residual connection to improve stability.

items.title: Muon momentum warmup
items.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 by about step 300, then hold it constant. Implement by computing the momentum value from the step counter each iteration and writing it into the Muon param group before the update. Leave all other optimizer settings unchanged.

items.title: Muon weight decay sweep to 0.1
items.spec: Lower the Muon decoupled weight decay from 0.2 to 0.1 and keep all other settings fixed. This tests whether the cautious masked weight decay on matrix parameters is too strong for a 300 s run that never approaches convergence. Only the WEIGHT_DECAY constant changes.

items.title: Muon weight decay sweep to 0.4
items.spec: Raise the Muon weight decay from 0.2 to 0.4 while leaving everything else untouched. This is the opposite direction of the 0.1 probe and tests whether stronger shrinkage of matrix weights helps generalization on the validation split. Only the WEIGHT_DECAY constant changes.

items.title: Gradient norm clipping
items.spec: Add global gradient norm clipping at 1.0 on all trainable parameters just before the optimizer step. Compute the norm with torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ over the parameter list. This guards against occasional loss spikes at the high Adam LR on embeddings and scalars.

items.title: Adam beta1 and epsilon for embeddings
items.spec: Use beta1 0.9 and epsilon 1e-10 for the embedding and unembedding Adam groups while keeping ADAM_BETAS (0.8, 0.95) for the scalar group. The sparse token-embedding gradients may benefit from a longer momentum window. Only the Adam parameter-group construction changes.

items.title: Newton-Schulz iteration count for Muon
items.spec: Increase the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside Muon from the current value to 6 for a more accurate polar factor. Keep the quintic coefficients as they are. Expect a small per-step time cost, so the net effect depends on the trade-off within the fixed wall-clock budget.

items.title: Cosine warmdown shape
items.spec: Replace the linear LR warmdown with a cosine decay from the peak LR to FINAL_LR_FRAC over the final WARMDOWN_RATIO fraction of the time budget. Compute progress from elapsed time over the budget, as the current schedule does. Everything before the warmdown is unchanged.

items.title: Longer warmdown ratio 0.7
items.spec: Extend the warmdown phase from WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 to 0.7 of the training time budget, so the LR starts decaying earlier and reaches its floor at the end. Keep the linear shape and the peak LRs unchanged. Only the WARMDOWN_RATIO constant changes.

items.title: Short linear warmup
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the LR ramps linearly from zero over the first 2 percent of the time budget before the existing schedule takes over. This avoids large early Muon and Adam updates on randomly initialized weights. Only the constant changes if the warmup code path already exists.

items.title: Non-zero final LR fraction
items.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 so the LR does not decay fully to zero at the end of the time budget. A small residual LR can keep the final steps useful when the schedule is cut by wall-clock time. Only the constant changes.

items.title: Batch size 2^18 for more steps
items.spec: Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 so that each optimizer step is cheaper and the 300 s budget yields roughly twice as many updates. Keep the per-device micro-batch and the gradient accumulation logic consistent with the new total. Learning rates are unchanged.

items.title: Batch size 2^20 for larger steps
items.spec: Double TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20 to reduce gradient noise per step at the cost of fewer updates in the fixed budget. Use gradient accumulation to keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at 64 without running out of memory. Learning rates are unchanged.

items.title: Batch size warmup
items.spec: Start training with a total batch of 2**17 tokens and grow it in powers of two to 2**19 over the first half of the time budget, using gradient accumulation to realize each size. Small early batches give more updates while the loss is still falling fast. Keep the LR schedule keyed to elapsed time.

items.title: Depth 10 with narrower aspect ratio
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO to 52 so the model dimension stays near 512 while adding two layers. Verify that HEAD_DIM still divides the model dimension evenly. This tests whether extra depth beats the current 8-layer width at the same parameter scale.

items.title: Shallow wide model
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 6 and ASPECT_RATIO to 85 so the model is shallower and wider with a similar parameter count. Adjust the number of heads to keep HEAD_DIM at 128 so attention shapes stay valid. This tests whether fewer sequential layers train faster within 300 s.

items.title: Full-attention window pattern
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from SSSL to SSLL so half of the layers attend over the full context instead of a quarter. Check that the final layer is still full attention as required by the pattern logic. The extra global attention may help the byte-level validation loss at small cost.

items.title: Rotary base frequency 100000
items.spec: Increase the RoPE base frequency from 10000 to 100000 for all rotary embeddings. A larger base gives longer effective wavelengths, which can help attention over the sliding window and the full-context layers. Change only the base constant used when precomputing the rotary cos and sin tables.

items.title: Logit soft-capping
items.spec: Apply a tanh soft cap to the final logits, computed as 15 * tanh(logits / 15), before the cross-entropy loss. This bounds extreme logits and stabilizes training at the high learning rates used here. Apply it only in the training loss path and keep the evaluation computation consistent with the model output.

items.title: QK normalization with learned temperature
items.spec: Apply RMS normalization to queries and keys per head before rotary embedding, and add a learnable per-head scalar that multiplies the attention logits, initialized to about 1.0. This keeps attention entropy controlled as the model scales. Only the attention module changes.

items.title: Input-to-output embedding tying
items.spec: Tie the token embedding matrix and the lm_head weight into one shared parameter so the model uses fewer parameters for the vocabulary projection. Remove the separate UNEMBEDDING_LR group and use EMBEDDING_LR for the shared weight, with the scale on the output projection adjusted for the tying. Keep all other layers unchanged.

items.title: U-Net style skip connections
items.spec: Add long skip connections that feed the output of the first half of the transformer blocks into the matching blocks in the second half through learned per-channel scalars. Initialize the scalars to zero so training starts from the current architecture. Only the forward pass of the model class changes.

items.title: SwiGLU MLP at matched parameters
items.spec: Replace the ReLU-squared MLP with a SwiGLU gated MLP whose hidden width is set to about 2/3 of the current expansion so the parameter count matches. Keep the same residual wiring and initialization scale style. This tests whether a gated feed-forward helps per unit of compute in the fixed time budget.

items.title: Zero-initialized residual output projections
items.spec: Initialize the output projection of every attention and MLP block to exactly zero so each block starts as an identity mapping and the network trains like a shallower model at first. Keep the input projections at their current initialization. Only the weight initialization code changes.

items.title: Z-loss regularization on logits
items.spec: Add an auxiliary loss of 1e-4 times the squared log-sum-exp of the logits, averaged over tokens, to the cross-entropy objective during training only. This keeps the softmax normalizer near zero and reduces logit drift. The reported validation loss is still computed as standard cross-entropy.

items.title: Weight decay on matrices only
items.spec: Confirm that Muon weight decay is applied only to two-dimensional matrix weights and that Adam groups for embeddings and per-layer scalars use zero weight decay. Remove any weight decay from the scalar and embedding parameter groups if present. This avoids shrinking parameters that need large magnitudes.

items.title: Linearly decayed weight decay
items.spec: Scale the Muon weight decay by the remaining fraction of the time budget so it decreases linearly from its initial value to zero at the end of training. Compute the fraction from elapsed time each step and write the scaled value into the Muon param group. Strong early regularization then relaxes as the LR shrinks.

items.title: Exponential moving average of weights
items.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of all trainable parameters with decay 0.999, updated after every optimizer step inside the training loop. Swap the averaged weights in only for the final evaluation pass that the harness already calls. Keep the training forward pass on the live weights and do not alter the evaluation code itself.

items.title: Document-boundary attention masking
items.spec: If the batch contains document boundary tokens, restrict attention so tokens cannot attend across a boundary and reset rotary positions at each new document. Build the mask from the BOS token positions already present in the input batch. This removes cross-document leakage in packed sequences during training.

items.title: Sequence length curriculum
items.spec: Begin training with a shorter context of 512 tokens and double it at fixed fractions of the time budget up to the full sequence length, adjusting the batch shape so the total token count per step is unchanged. Short early contexts allow faster steps and more updates. Keep the window pattern logic valid for each length.
