items.title: Muon momentum warmup
items.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Implement by computing the momentum value each step from the step counter and writing it into the Muon param group before the update. No other changes.

items.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations
items.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside the Muon update from 5 to 3. This saves compute per step, which buys more optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s budget. Leave learning rate and momentum unchanged.

items.title: Zero weight decay on embeddings and lm_head
items.spec: Set weight decay to 0 for the token embedding and lm_head (Adam-optimized) parameter groups while keeping WEIGHT_DECAY=0.2 for Muon matrix parameters. Only the per-group weight_decay field changes in the optimizer construction.

items.title: Shape-aware Muon LR scaling
items.spec: Scale each matrix parameter's Muon update learning rate by max(1, rows/cols)**0.5 (or equivalently sqrt(fan_out/fan_in)), so tall and wide matrices receive comparable update RMS. Apply this inside the Muon step using the parameter's shape; keep MATRIX_LR as the base value.

items.title: Global gradient-norm clipping
items.spec: Clip the global gradient norm of all trainable parameters to 1.0 immediately before optimizer.step() each iteration. This guards against occasional loss spikes at the high embedding LR of 0.6. Add a single torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ call.

items.title: Lower Adam beta1 for scalars and embeddings
items.spec: Use beta1=0.9 (beta2 kept at 0.95) only for the Adam groups covering embeddings, lm_head and per-layer scalars, leaving ADAM_BETAS as is for others if any remain. This tests whether a longer momentum horizon helps the noisy sparse embedding gradients.

items.title: Lower embedding LR
items.spec: Reduce EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3 while keeping all other learning rates unchanged. The current value is high and may cause instability or wasted capacity in the first steps; this tests a moderate setting.

items.title: Nesterov-free Muon with decoupled WD
items.spec: Switch the Muon update to plain momentum without Nesterov lookahead and apply weight decay as decoupled multiplicative decay p <- p*(1 - lr*WD) before the orthogonalized update. Keep MATRIX_LR and WEIGHT_DECAY values the same. Verify the decay is applied once per step.

items.title: Warmdown shape: sqrt instead of linear
items.spec: Keep the 0.5 time-fraction warmdown but change the decay curve from linear to a square-root shape: lr multiplier = sqrt(remaining_fraction) over the warmdown window. Apply this to all parameter groups identically.

items.title: Longer warmdown with small final LR
items.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.65 and FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.05 so the learning rate anneals over a larger share of the budget and does not reach exactly zero. Only the two constants change.

items.title: Short linear warmup
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so that the learning rate ramps linearly from 0 over the first 2% of the time budget before the warmdown begins. This is a small stability change for the high initial LRs.

items.title: WSD schedule with long stable phase
items.spec: Replace the current warmdown with a warmup-stable-decay schedule: linear warmup over 2% of the time budget, constant LR until 70% of the budget, then linear decay to 0 over the remaining 30%. Compute the phase from elapsed wall-clock time fraction.

items.title: Time-based EMA of weights for evaluation
items.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of model weights with decay 0.999 updated each step, and run the final validation pass with the EMA weights swapped in. Keep the training forward pass on the raw weights. Do not alter the evaluation call or summary printing.

items.title: Smaller total batch for more steps
items.spec: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 tokens per optimizer step. In a 300 s budget a small model is limited by step count, so this doubles the number of updates. Gradient accumulation adjusts automatically from DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE.

items.title: Batch-size ramp
items.spec: Start training with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**17 and double it at 30% and 60% of the time budget up to 2**19, implementing the change via gradient accumulation steps recomputed from the elapsed time fraction. Keep the learning rates fixed.

items.title: Smaller device batch with accumulation
items.spec: Set DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 and double the gradient accumulation steps so the effective TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE is unchanged. This lowers peak memory and may improve throughput through better cache behavior; it should not change the effective optimization.

items.title: Deeper, narrower model
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO to 52 so model_dim stays near the current width-by-depth budget while adding layers. Recompute head count from HEAD_DIM as already done. This tests whether extra depth helps at the same approximate parameter count.

items.title: Shallower, wider model
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 6 and ASPECT_RATIO to 80 so the model is wider and shallower with a similar parameter count. Head count is derived from HEAD_DIM as before. This tests whether faster per-step throughput outweighs reduced depth in the fixed time budget.

items.title: Squared-ReLU MLP activation
items.spec: Replace the MLP nonlinearity with squared ReLU (relu(x)**2) in the feed-forward blocks, keeping the hidden width and projections unchanged. This is a single activation swap that is often more sample-efficient than GELU for small GPTs.

items.title: QK-norm on queries and keys
items.spec: Apply RMS normalization to the query and key vectors per head before rotary embedding, with a learned per-head gain initialized to 1. This stabilizes attention logits at the high learning rates used here.

items.title: Value residual from first layer
items.spec: Add a learned-gated skip that mixes the first layer's value projection into the value vectors of every subsequent layer (ResFormer-style), with the mixing weight a learnable scalar per layer initialized to 0. This adds almost no parameters.

items.title: Logit soft-capping
items.spec: Apply logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15) before the cross-entropy loss to bound output logits. This is a numerical stabilizer that prevents runaway logits at the high LR; leave the rest of the model unchanged.

items.title: Higher RoPE base
items.spec: Increase the rotary embedding base from 10000 to 100000 so position frequencies vary more slowly across the context. Only the base constant in the rotary embedding construction changes.

items.title: Parallel attention and MLP blocks
items.spec: Change each transformer block to compute attention and the MLP from the same normalized input and add both outputs to the residual stream (GPT-J style parallel residual). Keep parameter count the same and retain the existing per-layer scalars.

items.title: Sliding-window pattern SSSSSL
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SSSSSL' so that a larger fraction of layers use short windows, with the final layer kept full. This reduces attention cost per step and may allow more steps in the budget.

items.title: Weight decay sweep to 0.1
items.spec: Reduce WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1 for the Muon matrix parameters. With only about 300 seconds of training the model is likely underfit, so less decay may help. Change only this constant.

items.title: Z-loss on output logits
items.spec: Add an auxiliary loss term 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)**2) to the training cross-entropy to keep the softmax normalizer from drifting. Compute it from the same logits tensor used for the main loss; evaluation loss remains unchanged.

items.title: No weight decay on norms and scalars
items.spec: Exclude per-layer scalar gains and any normalization parameters from weight decay, keeping decay only on Muon matrix weights. This is a parameter-group filter change in optimizer construction.

items.title: Sequence-length curriculum
items.spec: Train with a shorter effective context (for example 512 tokens, obtained by reshaping each batch into more sequences of half length) for the first 40% of the time budget, then switch to the full context length. Keep the token count per step unchanged. Evaluation still uses the full context.

items.title: Mask cross-document attention when boundaries are visible
items.spec: If the batch exposes document boundary tokens (BOS), build an attention mask so tokens cannot attend across document boundaries within a packed sequence, using only information present in the batch returned by the existing loader. Skip the change entirely if no boundary information is available in the loader output.

items.title: Compile and kernel settings
items.spec: Enable torch.compile with mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' for the model forward and confirm the attention path uses the fused scaled_dot_product_attention kernel with bf16 autocast. Startup time must stay well within the 450 s limit. This aims to increase throughput per second of training.

items.title: Fp32 master weights for embeddings
items.spec: Keep token embedding and lm_head parameters in fp32 while running the rest of the model under bf16 autocast, so the high-LR Adam updates on embeddings are not limited by bf16 precision. Only the dtype handling for those two modules changes.

items.title: Muon momentum warmup
items.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum from 0.85 at step 0 linearly up to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold 0.95. Apply the same schedule to every Muon parameter group. No other changes.

items.title: Disable Muon Nesterov momentum
items.spec: Set the Muon update to use plain momentum (nesterov=False) instead of Nesterov momentum, keeping the momentum coefficient and everything else the same. This isolates whether the Nesterov lookahead helps at this short training budget.

items.title: More Newton-Schulz iterations for Muon
items.spec: Increase the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside Muon from the current value to 6 (keep the existing quintic coefficients). This makes the update closer to an exact orthogonalization at a modest extra per-step cost.

items.title: Lower Muon matrix learning rate
items.spec: Reduce MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.02, leaving all other learning rates unchanged. Tests whether the Muon step size is too aggressive for the 300 s budget.

items.title: Higher Muon matrix learning rate
items.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06, leaving all other learning rates unchanged. Tests whether the short schedule benefits from larger orthogonalized updates.

items.title: Lower embedding learning rate
items.spec: Reduce EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3 for the token embedding Adam group, keeping the rest of the optimizer setup identical. Tests whether the large embedding step is hurting early convergence.

items.title: Adam beta2 = 0.99 for non-Muon groups
items.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.9, 0.99) for the Adam parameter groups (embeddings, lm_head, scalars). Muon parameters are unaffected.

items.title: Gradient norm clipping
items.spec: Add global gradient norm clipping at 1.0 on all trainable parameters after the backward pass and before the optimizer steps. Log nothing extra; only the clip call is added.

items.title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear
items.spec: Replace the linear learning-rate warmdown over the final WARMDOWN_RATIO of the time budget with a cosine decay from the peak LR to FINAL_LR_FRAC, applied to all optimizer groups multiplicatively. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO at 0.5.

items.title: Longer warmdown
items.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the learning rate decays over the last 70 percent of the time budget. Everything else is unchanged.

items.title: Short linear LR warmup
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so every learning-rate group ramps linearly from zero over the first 2 percent of the time budget before following the existing schedule. Muon momentum schedule is untouched.

items.title: Non-zero final learning rate
items.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 so the warmdown ends at 10 percent of the peak learning rate instead of zero. Keep all other settings identical.

items.title: Smaller total batch size
items.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 (about 262K tokens per step). This doubles the number of optimizer steps in the 300 s budget. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE and gradient accumulation logic consistent so the effective batch matches the new total.

items.title: Larger total batch size
items.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**20 (about 1M tokens per step), using gradient accumulation to reach it with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64. Fewer but larger steps for the same wall-clock budget.

items.title: Batch size ramp
items.spec: Start training with half of TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE and double it once at 50 percent of the time budget, using gradient accumulation steps computed from the current batch size each step. Learning rates are unchanged.

items.title: Logit soft-capping
items.spec: Apply a soft cap to the output logits before the cross-entropy loss: logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15). This bounds extreme logits and can stabilize the short high-LR run. Apply only in the training and evaluation forward pass that produces logits, identically in both.

items.title: QK-norm with learnable head gain
items.spec: After projecting queries and keys in each attention layer, RMS-normalize q and k per head and multiply each head by a learnable scalar gain initialized to 1. Keep rotary embeddings applied after normalization.

items.title: RoPE base 100000
items.spec: Change the rotary embedding base frequency from 10000 to 100000. Keep head dimension and everything else identical.

items.title: Head dimension 64
items.spec: Change HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64, which doubles the number of attention heads at the same model width. Everything else is unchanged.

items.title: All-long attention window
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "LLLL" so every layer uses full context. Keep the model size unchanged. Tests whether the sliding-window locality costs quality at this sequence length.

items.title: Deeper, narrower model
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO to 51 so model_dim stays near 512 while adding layers. Keep HEAD_DIM and other settings identical; check the rounded model_dim is divisible by HEAD_DIM.

items.title: Wider model
items.spec: Set ASPECT_RATIO to 80 with DEPTH 8, giving a wider model_dim of about 640. Round model_dim to a multiple of HEAD_DIM. Learning rates unchanged.

items.title: SwiGLU MLP
items.spec: Replace the MLP block with a SwiGLU gated MLP whose hidden width is about 2/3 of the usual 4x expansion (so parameter count is roughly matched), using silu(gate) * up followed by the down projection. Keep the residual structure unchanged.

items.title: Per-layer residual mixing with input embedding
items.spec: In each block, mix the running residual with the original token embedding x0 using two learnable per-layer scalars initialized to 1 and 0 (x = a*x + b*x0) before the attention and MLP sublayers. Scalars are optimized with the existing scalar Adam group.

items.title: Scaled output-projection init
items.spec: Initialize the attention output projection and MLP down projection weights with standard deviation divided by sqrt(2 * DEPTH) instead of the default, while keeping other initializations unchanged. This keeps residual stream variance controlled at the start of training.

items.title: Exponential moving average of weights
items.spec: Maintain an EMA copy of model parameters with decay 0.999 updated after each optimizer step, and use the EMA weights for the final validation forward pass only. Training dynamics are unchanged; the eval path is the existing one called on the EMA parameters.

items.title: Z-loss regularizer
items.spec: Add an auxiliary loss 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) to the cross-entropy during training only, to keep output logit normalizers from drifting. The reported training loss uses the cross-entropy term alone.

items.title: Zero weight decay on embeddings
items.spec: Set weight decay to zero on the token embedding and lm_head parameters while keeping WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2 on Muon matrices. Only decay selection changes.

items.title: Linearly decayed Muon weight decay
items.spec: Scale the Muon weight decay by the current learning-rate multiplier so it decays linearly to zero over the schedule instead of staying constant at WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2. Keep the initial value at 0.2.

items.title: Light dropout in attention and MLP
items.spec: Add dropout with probability 0.05 to attention output and MLP output before the residual additions, active only in training mode. Evaluation keeps dropout disabled as usual.

items.title: Sequence length curriculum
items.spec: Begin training with a sequence length of half the normal context and switch to the full length at 50 percent of the time budget, keeping the number of tokens per step equal by adjusting the batch dimension. Rotary and window logic must use the active length.

items.title: Increase Model Depth
items.spec: Increase the DEPTH variable from 8 to 12. Larger models usually capture more complex patterns, potentially lowering val_bpb despite having less time to train.

items.title: Increase Aspect Ratio
items.spec: Increase ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 128. This increases the model_dim (since model_dim = depth * ASPECT_RATIO), providing more capacity.

items.title: Reduce Head Dimension
items.spec: Decrease HEAD_DIM from 128 to 96. This might allow for more heads or a more compact representation of information.

items.title: Decrease Weight Decay
items.spec: Decrease WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1. High weight decay can sometimes over-regularize small models, preventing them from learning the data well enough.

items.title: Increase Matrix LR
items.spec: Increase MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.08. A higher learning rate for the primary weights (Muon) might lead to faster convergence in a short time window.

items.title: Decrease Matrix LR
items.spec: Decrease MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.02. If the model is diverging or oscillating, a smaller learning rate for the matrix weights might stabilize training.

items.title: Increase Embedding LR
items.spec: Increase EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.8. This speeds up the learning of the high-dimensional token embeddings.

items.title: Decrease Embedding LR
items.spec: Decrease EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.4. This prevents the embedding layer from being 'washed out' by large updates early on.

items.title: Increase Unembedding LR
items.spec: Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.01. This helps the lm_head map the internal representations to the correct vocabulary tokens faster.

items.title: Decrease Unembedding LR
items.spec: Decrease UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.002. Prevents catastrophic forgetting of the output distribution.

items.title: Increase Scalar LR
items.spec: Increase SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.7. Per-layer scalars (like layerNorm gains) often need aggressive updates to stabilize deep networks.

items.title: Decrease Scalar LR
items.spec: Decrease SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.3. Keeps the scaling factors more conservative.

items.title: Increase Warmdown Ratio
items.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7. A longer warmdown period allows the model to settle into a local minimum more smoothly.

items.title: Decrease Warmdown Ratio
items.spec: Decrease WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.3. This gives more time for high-learning-rate exploration.

items.title: Add Warmup Ratio
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.05. A small amount of warmup can prevent gradient explosions in the first few steps.

items.title: Set Final LR Fraction
items.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC from 0.0 to 0.01. Ensuring the learning rate doesn't hit absolute zero might allow for slightly more refinement at the very end.

items.title: Increase Total Batch Size
items.spec: Increase TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20. Larger global batches usually provide more stable gradients, provided they fit in memory (which they do since only DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE is limited).

items.title: Decrease Total Batch Size
items.spec: Decrease TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18. Smaller batches can sometimes provide more 'noise' which helps escape local minima in short runs.

items.title: Change Window Pattern
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "SSSS". This changes the sliding window proportions, potentially focusing more on local context.

items.title: Change Window Pattern 2
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "LLLL". This focuses more on long-range context dependencies.

items.title: Adjust Adam Betas
items.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.9, 0.99). These are more standard values for Adam and might provide smoother updates for the non-Muon parameters.

items.title: Modify Adam Beta1
items.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.7, 0.95). A smaller beta1 can make the optimizer more reactive to recent gradients.

items.title: Modify Adam Beta2
items.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.8, 0.999). A larger beta2 maintains a longer history of the squared gradients.

items.title: Decrease Aspect Ratio (Thin)
items.spec: Decrease ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 32. This makes the model 'thinner' (lower dimension) but maintains the depth. This might be faster to train and allow for more iterations.

items.title: Double Depth
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 16. Doubling the number of layers significantly increases the expressive power of the model.

items.title: Weight Decay for all
items.spec: Apply weight decay to all parameters by modifying how the optimizer is initialized or the hyperparameters, but specifically just changing WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.1.

items.title: Extreme Weight Decay
items.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.4. Use this if the model is severely overfitting the training data in a short amount of time.

items.title: Higher Unembedding LR
items.spec: Set UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.02. Very high learning rate on the head to force fast adaptation to the vocabulary.

items.title: Balanced Matrix LR
items.spec: Set MATRIX_LR to 0.02. A more conservative matrix learning rate to ensure stability over the 300s window.

items.title: Max Depth
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 24. Push the limits of what the 300s wall-clock time can train in a single run.

items.title: Muon momentum warmup
items.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Change only the momentum value fed to the Muon optimizer each step; leave all other Muon settings, the LR schedule and the Adam groups untouched.

items.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz steps in Muon
items.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside the Muon update from 5 to 3. This cuts optimizer overhead per step, which gives more optimizer steps inside the fixed 300 s budget. Keep the coefficients and everything else the same.

items.title: Shape-aware Muon update scale
items.spec: Scale each Muon orthogonalized update by sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) (or equivalently 0.2*sqrt(max(rows, cols)) so the update RMS matches AdamW), so that one MATRIX_LR works across the attention and MLP matrices of different shapes. Apply the scale inside the Muon step only; do not change MATRIX_LR unless a separate run requires it.

items.title: Small weight decay on Adam-managed parameters
items.spec: Add decoupled weight decay of 0.01 (scaled by the current LR multiplier) to the Adam parameter groups for token embeddings, lm_head and per-layer scalars. Leave the Muon weight decay unchanged. Implement by adding a weight_decay argument to the Adam param-group construction.

items.title: Per-group LR multiplier for attention vs MLP
items.spec: Split the Muon matrix parameters into attention (Q, K, V, output projection) and MLP groups, and multiply the LR of the attention group by 0.7 while leaving the MLP group at MATRIX_LR. Rationale: attention projections are often more sensitive to large steps. Keep the optimizer type and momentum identical.

items.title: Global gradient-norm clipping
items.spec: Before each optimizer step, call torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ on all model parameters with max_norm 1.0. Log nothing extra. This stabilizes the early high-LR phase at the cost of one norm computation per step.

items.title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear
items.spec: Replace the linear LR warmdown with a cosine decay: multiplier = 0.5*(1+cos(pi*p)) where p is the fraction of the warmdown window elapsed, applied to all parameter groups. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO and FINAL_LR_FRAC as they are.

items.title: Longer warmdown (ratio 0.7)
items.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.7 so the LR begins decaying at 30% of the time budget instead of 50%. All other schedule and optimizer settings stay the same. Tests whether a longer anneal improves the final bpb at this short training length.

items.title: Short linear warmup
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.03 so the LR ramps linearly from near zero over the first 3% of the time budget before the existing warmdown logic. This protects the early steps when Muon and the large Adam LRs (EMBEDDING_LR 0.6, SCALAR_LR 0.5) are most unstable.

items.title: Hold Adam LRs constant, anneal only Muon
items.spec: Keep the Adam-group LRs (embedding, lm_head, scalars) constant at their initial values for the whole run, and apply the warmdown multiplier only to the Muon matrix LR. Implement by excluding Adam groups from the schedule multiplier loop.

items.title: Non-zero final LR fraction
items.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 so the LR anneals to 10% of its peak rather than to zero. This is a single-constant change that tests whether a small residual LR helps the last steps at the cost of slightly less annealing.

items.title: Linearly decayed weight decay
items.spec: Multiply WEIGHT_DECAY (the Muon cautious weight decay) by the same time-based progress factor that drives the LR warmdown, so it decays linearly from 0.2 at the start to 0 at the end of training. Compute the factor from elapsed time at each step.

items.title: Output z-loss regularizer
items.spec: Add an auxiliary term 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits, dim=-1)^2) to the cross-entropy training loss to keep the output logit normalizer near zero. Apply only to the training loss; the evaluation function is not modified.

items.title: Tanh logit soft-capping
items.spec: Apply logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15) to the lm_head output before the cross-entropy loss in training (and in the model forward used by evaluation, since it is part of the model). This bounds extreme logits and often stabilizes short high-LR runs.

items.title: Smaller total batch (2^18 tokens)
items.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 so each optimizer step covers about 262K tokens. Gradient accumulation adjusts automatically from DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE. This doubles the number of optimizer steps in the 300 s budget; keep the learning rates unchanged for the first replicate.

items.title: Batch-size ramp
items.spec: Start with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**17 for the first 25% of the time budget, then 2**18 until 60%, then 2**19 for the rest. Adjust gradient accumulation steps at each boundary. Early small batches give more updates while the loss is high.

items.title: Sequence-length curriculum
items.spec: Train on shorter sequences first: use context length 512 for the first 30% of the time budget and the full MAX_SEQ_LEN for the rest, keeping the number of tokens per step constant by increasing the number of sequences per batch. Only the data slicing in the training loop changes; the evaluation path is untouched.

items.title: Deeper, narrower model (depth 10)
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO to 51 so model_dim is about 512 (depth*aspect rounded to a multiple of HEAD_DIM). This trades width for an extra layer at similar parameter count. Keep all other hyperparameters the same.

items.title: Initial-embedding skip connections
items.spec: Store the normalized token embedding x0 after the first layer and add a learned per-layer scalar times x0 into the residual stream at the input of every block (x = x + lambda_l * x0). Initialize lambda_l to 0.1. Adds one scalar per layer and no matrices.

items.title: Squared-ReLU MLP activation
items.spec: Replace the MLP activation with relu(x)**2 (squared ReLU) in place of the current nonlinearity. Keep the MLP width and projection shapes unchanged so only the activation changes.

items.title: Parallel attention and MLP blocks
items.spec: Change each transformer block to compute x = x + attn(norm(x)) + mlp(norm(x)) using a single shared pre-norm, instead of the sequential residual form. Keep weights and per-layer dimensions identical so parameter count does not change.

items.title: Window pattern alternative
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "SSSSSL" so most layers use half-context sliding windows and only the last layer is full attention. Keep DEPTH consistent with the pattern length (use 6 or 12 layers as required) or pad the pattern to DEPTH. Only the attention window schedule changes.

items.title: Higher RoPE base
items.spec: Increase the rotary embedding base from 10000 to 100000 so the position frequencies are lower and longer-range position information is preserved within the context. Only the rotary frequency computation changes.

items.title: Narrower MLP (3x expansion)
items.spec: Set the MLP hidden size to 3*model_dim instead of 4*model_dim and reinvest the saved parameters by keeping everything else identical. This reduces per-step FLOPs, letting more steps run in the fixed 300 s budget.

items.title: Learnable per-head QK scale
items.spec: After QK normalization, multiply queries and keys by a learnable per-head scalar initialized to 1.0 before the attention dot product. Add one scalar per head per layer to the Adam scalar group. No other shape changes.

items.title: Depth-scaled residual initialization
items.spec: Initialize the output projection of each attention and MLP block with standard deviation scaled by 1/sqrt(2*DEPTH) (GPT-2 style residual scaling), keeping all other initialization unchanged. This keeps the residual stream variance stable as depth grows.

items.title: EMA weights for evaluation
items.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of model parameters with decay 0.999 updated after each optimizer step, and swap the EMA weights into the model just before the final evaluation call. Do not modify the evaluation function itself; only the parameters it sees change.

items.title: Throughput: compile and attention backend
items.spec: Check that the model uses bf16 autocast and PyTorch scaled_dot_product_attention with the flash backend, and try torch.compile with mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs" for the model forward. Verify the startup-plus-training total stays under 450 s. The goal is more tokens processed per second inside the fixed training window.

items.title: Mask loss on document-start tokens
items.spec: Exclude from the training loss the prediction targets that immediately follow a BOS token (set their loss weight to 0), so the model is not penalized for predicting the first token of a new document from unrelated context. Implement as a mask built from the input ids using the BOS id already available in train.py. Evaluation is not changed.

items.title: RMSProp/AdamW Hybrid
items.spec: Switch the matrix optimizer from Muon to AdamW with a learning rate of 0.04 and weight decay of 0.01. This simplifies the optimizer state and might stabilize training for smaller models.

items.title: Muon Weight Decay Reduction
items.spec: Reduce the WEIGHT_DECAY for the Muon optimizer from 0.2 to 0.05. High weight decay can sometimes over-regularize small models, hindering their ability to memorize patterns.

items.title: Increase Depth, Decrease Aspect Ratio
items.spec: Change DEPTH to 12 and ASPECT_RATIO to 32 (keeping model_dim constant). This creates a 'deeper' model which often generalizes better for the same parameter count.

items.title: Decrease Aspect Ratio
items.spec: Change ASPECT_RATIO to 32. This reduces the width of the layers, potentially allowing for more expressive depth or better information flow in a small model.

items.title: Increase Aspect Ratio
items.spec: Change ASPECT_RATIO to 128. This creates a wider, shallower model. Wider models can sometimes capture more variety in the training data more quickly.

items.title: Linear LR Warmup
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.1. Adding a short warmup period can prevent gradient spikes in the first few iterations and lead to more stable convergence.

items.title: Aggressive LR Warmdown
items.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.7. A longer decay at the end of the 300s budget can help the model settle into a local minimum and refine the val_bpb.

items.title: Final LR Fraction Adjustment
items.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1. This ensures that the model continues to learn slightly even at the very end of the budget rather than dropping to zero too abruptly.

items.title: Increase Matrix LR
items.spec: Increase MATRIX_LR to 0.06. Since Muon is used for matrix parameters, a higher learning rate might accelerate the acquisition of structural features.

items.title: Decrease Scalar LR
items.spec: Decrease SCALAR_LR to 0.3. This slows down the adaptation of per-layer scalars, making the training more stable and less prone to 'blowing up' specific layers.

items.title: Embedding LR Boost
items.spec: Increase EMBEDDING_LR to 1.0. This allows the model to learn the vocabulary mappings faster, which is crucial in a short 300s training window.

items.title: Unembedding LR Boost
items.spec: Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.02. This speeds up the learning of the output heads, which is critical for minimizing bits per byte.

items.title: Increase Device Batch Size
items.spec: Increase DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 96. If it fits in 40GB, a larger batch size improves gradient stability and helps the model see more variety per step.

items.title: Decrease Device Batch Size
items.spec: Decrease DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 48. A smaller batch size (with higher total_batch_size if adjusted) can sometimes lead to better generalization on small datasets.

items.title: Total Batch Size Scaling
items.spec: Adjust TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE constant. This changes the global gradient averaging per step.

items.title: Head Dimension Expansion
items.spec: Increase HEAD_DIM to 256. This increases the capacity of the attention mechanism to represent complex relationships between tokens.

items.title: Head Dimension Contraction
items.spec: Decrease HEAD_DIM to 64. This allows for more heads (if the framework handles it) or simply keeps the attention mechanism more focused on local patterns.

items.title: Mixed Precision Training
items.spec: If the harness allows, implement automatic mixed precision (AMP) or explicitly use float16/bfloat16 for matrix multiplications to increase throughput.

items.title: Weight Decay for Scalars
items.spec: Apply weight decay to the scalar parameters by adding them to the Muon optimizer's weight decay or setting a separate small decay value.

items.title: No Warmdown
items.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.0. Use the full 300s for high-learning-rate exploration.

items.title: Deep Residual Connections
items.spec: Modify the model architecture to use a deeper residual structure (e.g., Pre-LN) if the current `train.py` allows architectural swaps.

items.title: RMSNorm Implementation
items.spec: Replace standard LayerNorm with RMSNorm (if the `train.py` implementation allows) to improve training stability and speed.

items.title: Learning Rate Scaling
items.spec: Scale all learning rates (EMBEDDING_LR, UNEMBEDDING_LR, MATRIX_LR, SCALAR_LR) by a factor of 0.8 to find a more conservative, stable equilibrium.

items.title: Specific Embedding Decay
items.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.0 for matrix parameters but maintain it for scalars to see if decoupling improves convergence.

items.title: Large Matrix LR / Small Scalar LR
items.spec: Set MATRIX_LR to 0.08 and SCALAR_LR to 0.1. This prioritizes learning the weight matrices while being very cautious with normalization scalars.

items.title: Window Pattern Change
items.spec: If WINDOW_PATTERN is configurable, change it from 'SSSL' to 'SSSS' to increase the amount of 'S' (half-context) processing.

items.title: Asymmetric LR
items.spec: Set EMBEDDING_LR to 0.2 and UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.01. This slows down the learning of the lookup tables to prevent overfitting the vocabulary early.

items.title: Weight Decay for Embeddings
items.spec: Introduce a small weight decay (0.01) specifically for the embedding layer weights.

items.title: Quick Finish Schedule
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.0 and WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.1. Focus 90% of the budget on high-intensity learning.

items.title: Model Shrinking
items.spec: Reduce DEPTH to 6. A smaller model might actually generalize better on very small datasets by avoiding over-parameterization.

items.title: Muon momentum warmup
items.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold it at 0.95. Change only the momentum value fed to the Muon update each step; leave MATRIX_LR, weight decay and the Newton-Schulz iterations untouched.

items.title: Shape-aware Muon LR scaling
items.spec: Scale the per-matrix Muon update by sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) so tall projection matrices (MLP up-projection, fan-out layers) get a proportionally larger step. Keep MATRIX_LR at 0.04 as the base; this only changes the per-parameter multiplier inside the Muon step.

items.title: Lower Adam beta1 for embeddings
items.spec: Use beta1=0.9 (instead of ADAM_BETAS[0]=0.8) for the embedding and lm_head Adam groups only, keeping beta2=0.95 and the scalar group at 0.8. The goal is less noisy embedding updates at the high EMBEDDING_LR of 0.6.

items.title: Embedding LR sweep down
items.spec: Reduce EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3 and keep UNEMBEDDING_LR at 0.004 and SCALAR_LR at 0.5. This tests whether the very high embedding learning rate is overshooting; no other code changes.

items.title: Newton-Schulz coefficient set
items.spec: Replace the Muon orthogonalization coefficients with the Polar-Express-style tuned quintic coefficients (a,b,c) per iteration while keeping 5 iterations. Only the constants inside the Newton-Schulz routine change; the surrounding Muon momentum and LR logic stays identical.

items.title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear
items.spec: Replace the linear LR warmdown over the last WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.5 of the time budget with a cosine decay from 1.0 to FINAL_LR_FRAC (0.0) applied to all parameter groups. Warmup stays at WARMUP_RATIO=0.0.

items.title: Longer warmdown
items.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the LR begins decaying at 30% of the time budget, keeping the linear shape and FINAL_LR_FRAC=0.0. Purely a hyperparameter change.

items.title: Short linear warmup
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the LR ramps linearly from 0 to its peak over the first 2% of the time budget (about 6 s) before the existing warmdown logic. Apply the ramp to all parameter groups.

items.title: Sqrt-shaped warmdown
items.spec: Change the warmdown multiplier to sqrt(remaining_fraction) over the final WARMDOWN_RATIO of the budget, so the LR stays higher for longer and drops steeply at the end. Keep FINAL_LR_FRAC=0.0 and all group base LRs as they are.

items.title: Smaller model dim, deeper net
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO to 48 so model_dim = 480 (rounded to a multiple of HEAD_DIM where needed), trading width for depth at roughly similar parameter count. Keep the rest of the configuration unchanged.

items.title: Wider, shallower model
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 6 and ASPECT_RATIO to 80 so the model is wider and shallower with similar compute per token; this also speeds steps so more tokens fit in 300 s. Keep HEAD_DIM=128 so the number of heads grows accordingly.

items.title: Logit soft-capping
items.spec: Apply logit soft-capping before the cross-entropy: logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15) at the lm_head output. This bounds extreme logits and stabilizes the high-LR embedding/unembedding training. Affects training and evaluation logits identically.

items.title: Value embedding residual on alternate layers
items.spec: Add a learned per-layer value residual: for every other attention layer, mix the token embedding (through a small learnable gate initialized to 0) into the value projection input. Adds only a few scalar parameters plus a reuse of the existing embedding table.

items.title: Learnable per-layer residual scales
items.spec: Initialize a learnable scalar on each residual branch (attention and MLP outputs) to 1/sqrt(2*DEPTH) and optimize it with the existing SCALAR_LR group. This replaces fixed residual scaling with a learned depth-aware scale.

items.title: Full attention in all layers
items.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN to "LLLL" so every layer uses full context instead of the SSSL sliding pattern. Only the window-pattern string changes; check that the window schedule still handles the final layer.

items.title: Rotary base increase
items.spec: Raise the RoPE base frequency from 10000 to 100000 for the rotary embeddings used in attention. This changes the position encoding wavelengths only, with no new parameters.

items.title: Bigram hash embedding
items.spec: Add a second small embedding table indexed by a hash of the previous token and current token (table size about 2^14 rows, dimension equal to model_dim with zero init) and add its output to the token embedding before the first block. Use the EMBEDDING_LR Adam group for it.

items.title: Parallel attention and MLP block
items.spec: Compute attention and MLP from the same normalized input and sum both outputs into the residual stream (GPT-J style parallel block) instead of sequential attn-then-MLP. Keep parameter counts and norms unchanged.

items.title: Squared-ReLU to GeGLU MLP
items.spec: Replace the MLP activation with a gated GeGLU (two up-projections, GELU gate, down-projection) and scale hidden width to 2/3 of the 4x expansion so parameter count stays the same. Muon still handles all three matrices.

items.title: Smaller total batch
items.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 (about 262K tokens per step) so the 300 s budget yields twice as many optimizer steps. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE and the LR values unchanged, adjusting only gradient accumulation.

items.title: Larger total batch
items.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**20 (about 1M tokens per step) with gradient accumulation to match, and scale MATRIX_LR up by sqrt(2) to 0.057 to compensate. Tests whether lower gradient noise pays for fewer steps.

items.title: Batch size ramp
items.spec: Start the effective batch at 2**17 tokens and double it at 25% and 60% of the time budget up to TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE=2**19, using gradient accumulation to reach each size. Keep LRs fixed; the accumulation count is recomputed from the current size.

items.title: Weight decay linear decay
items.spec: Linearly decay WEIGHT_DECAY on the Muon matrices from 0.2 at the start of training to 0.0 at the end of the time budget, instead of holding it constant. Only the per-step weight decay value changes.

items.title: Z-loss on logits
items.spec: Add an auxiliary penalty 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) to the training loss to keep output logit normalizers small. Do not include this term in the evaluation loss path; only the training objective changes.

items.title: Embedding dropout
items.spec: Apply dropout with p=0.05 to the token embedding output during training only (disabled in eval mode). This is a light regularizer on the input representation with no extra parameters.

items.title: Sequence length curriculum
items.spec: Train with half the configured sequence length for the first 40% of the time budget, then switch to the full sequence length, keeping tokens per step constant by adjusting the batch of sequences. Data loading must still use only the existing harness-provided loader.

items.title: Document-start aligned batches
items.spec: Ensure each training sequence starts at a document boundary where the loader provides one (or resets attention at the boundary if it is cheap to do so), reducing cross-document context noise. Only the sampling/packing code in the training loop changes; the eval path is untouched.

items.title: Weight EMA for final model
items.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of model parameters with decay 0.999 updated each step, and use the EMA weights for the final model state only if they are the ones evaluated by the training script's own forward path. Do not alter the evaluation call itself.

items.title: Late checkpoint averaging
items.spec: Average parameter snapshots taken every 50 steps during the final 20% of the time budget (uniform average) and load the averaged weights before the final evaluation. Overhead is one parameter copy per snapshot; memory stays under the 40 GB limit by storing snapshots on CPU.

items.title: Compile and precision throughput
items.spec: Enable torch.compile with mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs" for the model forward and set torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=True plus high matmul precision for any fp32 matmuls. Goal is more tokens processed within the fixed 300 s budget; numerics should be unchanged apart from precision flags.

items.title: Muon momentum warmup
items.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Keep everything else (Nesterov, LR, weight decay) unchanged. Implement by computing the momentum value from the step counter each iteration and writing it into the Muon param groups before the step.

items.title: Muon momentum cooldown in warmdown
items.spec: Keep Muon momentum at 0.95 for the first part of training, then lower it linearly to 0.85 during the warmdown phase (the last WARMDOWN_RATIO of the time budget). This lets the late low-LR phase take smaller, less noisy steps. Update the momentum value in the Muon param groups each step based on elapsed-time fraction.

items.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations
items.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations in the Muon update from 5 to 3. This cuts optimizer overhead per step, so more steps fit in the fixed 300 s budget. Keep the quintic coefficients consistent with the reduced iteration count, or retune them if the code uses fixed per-iteration coefficients. Leave all LRs unchanged.

items.title: Adam epsilon and scalar-group tuning
items.spec: Lower the Adam epsilon for the embedding, unembedding, and scalar parameter groups from the default 1e-8 to 1e-10. Hidden-state scalars and embeddings have small gradients in this setup, so a smaller eps can speed their updates. Change only the eps argument in the Adam constructor; leave betas and LRs unchanged.

items.title: Separate LR for attention vs MLP Muon matrices
items.spec: Split the Muon matrix parameters into two groups: attention projection matrices (Q, K, V, O) use MATRIX_LR * 0.8 and MLP matrices use MATRIX_LR * 1.2. Keep the same momentum, weight decay, and Newton-Schulz settings for both groups. This tests whether the two blocks prefer different effective step sizes.

items.title: Matrix LR sweep upward
items.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06 and leave all other hyperparameters unchanged. Muon with orthogonalized updates often tolerates larger LRs than the default, and the short 300 s budget favors faster early progress. This is a single-value change intended to find the upper side of the LR optimum.

items.title: Embedding weight decay
items.spec: Apply a small decoupled weight decay of 0.01 to the Adam-optimized embedding and unembedding parameters, which currently receive no decay. Implement by setting weight_decay=0.01 in the Adam param groups for those tensors only. Keep the Muon weight decay of 0.2 unchanged for matrix parameters.

items.title: Weight decay linear decay to zero
items.spec: Scale the Muon weight decay with the schedule: at each step set the effective WEIGHT_DECAY to its base value of 0.2 multiplied by (1 - elapsed_fraction), so decay falls linearly to zero by the end of the 300 s budget. This keeps regularization strong early and lets the model fit fully at the end. Implement by updating the weight_decay field of the Muon param groups each step.

items.title: Gradient clipping
items.spec: Add global gradient-norm clipping at 1.0 after the backward pass and before the optimizer steps. Use torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ over all trainable parameters. This guards against occasional loss spikes at the high peak LRs used for the scalar and embedding groups.

items.title: Logit z-loss
items.spec: Add an auxiliary z-loss term 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits, dim=-1)^2) to the training cross-entropy loss, computed over the unembedding logits. This keeps output logits from drifting in magnitude and is known to stabilize training at higher LRs. The term applies only to the training loss; the evaluation path must remain unchanged.

items.title: Longer warmdown with cosine shape
items.spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine decay: multiply the LR by 0.5*(1+cos(pi*p)) where p is elapsed-time fraction over the warmdown window, and keep WARMDOWN_RATIO at 0.5. Set the constant-LR phase before warmdown unchanged. Apply the same multiplier to all parameter groups.

items.title: Extended warmdown ratio
items.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the learning rate begins decaying earlier and spends more of the budget in the annealing regime. Keep the linear shape and FINAL_LR_FRAC at 0.0. This is a single-value change testing whether a longer anneal improves final val_bpb for a short run.

items.title: Short warmup at start
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the LR ramps linearly from 0 over the first 2% of the time budget before any decay. The current baseline starts at full LR, which can destabilize early Muon updates at high LR. Apply the same linear ramp multiplier to all parameter groups.

items.title: Final LR floor
items.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.05 so the LR decays to 5% of its initial value rather than to zero at the end of the budget. Keep the warmdown ratio unchanged. This is a single-value change that tests whether a small nonzero final LR helps the last few steps.

items.title: Batch size halved for more steps
items.spec: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 tokens per optimizer step, keeping DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE and the gradient accumulation logic so that accumulation steps halve. In a 300 s budget this doubles the number of optimizer updates. Keep all LRs unchanged for this single-value test.

items.title: Batch size ramp
items.spec: Start training with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**17 and double it at 25%, 50%, and 75% of the time budget up to 2**19, adjusting gradient accumulation steps each time. Smaller early batches give many cheap updates when the loss is high, and larger batches later reduce gradient noise. Recompute the number of accumulation steps from the current batch size at each boundary.

items.title: Head dimension 64
items.spec: Change HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64, which doubles the number of attention heads at fixed model width. Keep model_dim, DEPTH, and ASPECT_RATIO unchanged so parameter count is nearly identical. Smaller heads are often more efficient per FLOP for short training, and the sliding-window attention pattern is unaffected.

items.title: Deeper narrower model
items.spec: Set DEPTH to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO to 52 so model_dim (depth times aspect ratio) stays near 512 and parameter count is roughly matched while adding two layers. Keep HEAD_DIM and WINDOW_PATTERN unchanged. This tests whether extra depth helps more than the lost width at this scale.

items.title: Value residual from first layer
items.spec: Add a ResFormer-style value residual: compute each layer's attention value projection and mix it with the first layer's value output using a learnable per-layer scalar initialized to 0.5. Only the first layer's values are reused, so this adds one scalar per layer and no new matrices. Keep all other architecture details unchanged.

items.title: SwiGLU MLP
items.spec: Replace the MLP's squared-ReLU block with a SwiGLU block: two up-projections of width 8/3 times model_dim (rounded to a multiple of 64), a SiLU gate, and a down-projection. Pick the hidden width so total MLP parameters are close to the original 4x expansion. Keep attention and normalization unchanged.

items.title: QK-norm with learnable gain
items.spec: Apply RMS normalization to queries and keys per head, each with a learnable per-head scalar gain initialized to 1.0, before rotary embedding is applied. This bounds attention logit scale and allows slightly higher LRs without instability. Add only the gain parameters; the normalization itself is parameter-free.

items.title: Rotary base frequency
items.spec: Increase the rotary embedding base from 10000 to 100000. A larger base lowers the frequency of the rotary components, which can help attention over the longer sliding-window context used by the full-attention layers. Change only the base constant in the rotary embedding module.

items.title: Sliding window pattern change
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "SSSSSL" so only one in six layers uses full context and most layers use half-context sliding windows. This lowers attention compute per step and may let the model take more steps in the time budget. If the code requires the pattern length to divide DEPTH, keep DEPTH at 8 and use "SSSL" repeated as the code expects, or otherwise adjust minimally.

items.title: Residual scalars init
items.spec: Initialize the per-layer residual mixing scalars so that the skip contribution starts at 1.0 and the block output starts at 0.1 times its value, rather than the current initialization. Only the initial values of these learnable scalars change, not their LRs or the optimizer grouping. This tests whether a gentler start helps the deeper residual stream.

items.title: Untied token embedding init scale
items.spec: Scale the token embedding initialization standard deviation by 0.5 relative to the current value and leave the unembedding (lm_head) initialization unchanged. Smaller initial embedding norms reduce early logit magnitudes and may let the high embedding LR (0.6, Adam) take steadier early steps. Only the init scale changes.

items.title: Exponential moving average for evaluation
items.spec: Maintain an EMA copy of the model parameters with decay 0.999, updated after each optimizer step during the final 50% of the time budget. Use the EMA weights for the final evaluation pass only, by copying them into the model before the existing evaluation call. Do not alter the evaluation function or summary printing; only swap the weights in before those calls.

items.title: Adaptive sequence length curriculum
items.spec: Train the first 30% of the time budget on half-length sequences and then switch to full length. Shorter sequences give cheaper steps early when the model learns coarse structure. Keep the total tokens per optimizer step unchanged by doubling the number of sequences per micro-batch during the short-sequence phase, and reset data iteration cleanly at the switch point.

items.title: Attention and compile efficiency check
items.spec: Enable a faster matmul precision setting (torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('high')) and wrap the training forward with torch.compile using mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' if compile is already used. Keep all model math and the evaluation path unchanged. This only changes throughput, so any gain comes from more steps in the fixed time budget.

items.title: Logit softcap check
items.spec: Apply a tanh soft cap to the output logits at 15, computing logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15) before the cross-entropy loss, if the current model does not already do so. The cap bounds extreme logits that can dominate early loss and destabilize high-LR training. Apply the cap in the training forward path only, and keep the evaluation call unchanged.

The cap bounds extreme logits that can dominate early loss and destabilize high-LR training. Apply the cap in the training forward path only, and keep the evaluation call unchanged.","family":"regularization"}]}

items.title: Muon momentum warmup
items.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Change only the momentum schedule for the Muon param group; leave all other hyperparameters as they are.

items.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon
items.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside Muon from 5 to 3. This saves wall-clock per step, so more steps fit in the 300 s budget. Keep the quintic coefficients unchanged unless the orthogonalization becomes unstable.

items.title: Zero weight decay on embedding and lm_head
items.spec: Set weight decay to 0 for the token embedding and lm_head parameters, which use Adam. Keep WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.2 only for the Muon matrix parameters. Implement this by splitting the Adam param groups so the embedding and unembedding groups carry weight_decay=0.

items.title: Linearly decayed Muon weight decay
items.spec: Make the Muon weight decay schedule-dependent: start at WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.2 and decay linearly to 0.0 by the end of the time budget, using the same progress fraction that drives the LR schedule. Apply the multiplier each step to the Muon group's weight_decay.

items.title: Shape-aware Muon learning rate scaling
items.spec: Scale the Muon update per matrix by sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) so tall and wide matrices get comparable effective step sizes. Keep MATRIX_LR = 0.04 as the base value. Apply the scale factor per parameter when building the update, without changing the orthogonalization itself.

items.title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear
items.spec: Replace the linear LR warmdown with a cosine decay over the warmdown portion. Keep the warmdown starting point at WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.5 of the time budget and the final LR at FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.0. Use lr = base * 0.5 * (1 + cos(pi * t)) where t runs from 0 to 1 over the warmdown.

items.title: Short LR warmup
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.02 so that the learning rate ramps linearly from zero over the first 2 percent of the time budget before the schedule plateau. This guards against instability from the high Adam LR on embeddings (0.6) and the large Muon LR.

items.title: Longer warmdown
items.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the LR decays over most of the run. Keep the linear shape and FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.0. This tests whether a longer anneal improves the final bits per byte within the fixed 300 s budget.

items.title: Nonzero final LR fraction
items.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05 so the LR does not reach zero at the end of training. Keep all other schedule settings unchanged. The final steps then still make useful updates instead of wasting the last part of the budget.

items.title: Smaller total batch size
items.spec: Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 tokens per optimizer step. This doubles the number of optimizer steps in the fixed time budget. Gradient accumulation should be adjusted so DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 64 still fits, with accumulation steps halved.

items.title: Batch size ramp
items.spec: Start TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE at 2**17 tokens and double it at 1/3 and 2/3 of the time budget up to 2**19. Compute the accumulation steps from the current batch size on each step. Early steps get more updates while later steps get lower gradient noise.

items.title: Larger total batch size
items.spec: Double TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20 tokens per optimizer step. Increase gradient accumulation accordingly while keeping DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 64. Keep the LRs unchanged. This tests whether lower gradient noise beats the loss of step count in the time budget.

items.title: Shallower wider model
items.spec: Set DEPTH = 6 and ASPECT_RATIO = 85 so the model dimension is about 510 with 6 layers. Keep HEAD_DIM = 128. The model then runs more tokens per second, which may help within the fixed 300 s budget. Round model_dim to a multiple of HEAD_DIM.

items.title: Deeper narrower model
items.spec: Set DEPTH = 10 and ASPECT_RATIO = 51 so model_dim is about 510 with 10 layers. Keep HEAD_DIM = 128 and round model_dim to a multiple of HEAD_DIM. The extra depth may improve per-token quality at a modest throughput cost.

items.title: Smaller attention head dimension
items.spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 so each model has twice as many attention heads at the same model_dim. Keep the rest of the attention code unchanged. This tests whether more heads improve modeling quality at the same parameter count.

items.title: Full attention in all layers
items.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "L" so every layer uses full causal context instead of the sliding-window pattern. Check that memory still fits in 40 GB at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 64. This tests whether the sliding windows lose useful context at this short training length.

items.title: U-Net style skip connections
items.spec: Add learned skip connections from the output of the first half of layers to the input of the mirrored layers in the second half. Each skip uses a per-channel learnable scalar initialized to zero, and is added before each block's attention. This gives the decoder layers direct access to early representations.

items.title: Parallel attention and MLP residual
items.spec: Compute the attention and MLP branches of each block from the same normalized input and add both to the residual stream in one step, as in GPT-J. Keep the per-layer scalars and the norm placement otherwise unchanged. This reduces the sequential depth of each block and may speed up each step.

items.title: Per-head learnable attention scale
items.spec: Add a learnable scalar per attention head that multiplies the query-key logits after QK normalization. Initialize it to 1.0 and train it with the scalar Adam group at SCALAR_LR. This lets each head adjust its sharpness without changing the attention scale globally.

items.title: Lower logit softcap
items.spec: Change the logit soft-capping value from its current setting to 15 by applying logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15) before the cross-entropy loss. Keep everything else the same. A tighter cap may stabilize the high learning rate on the unembedding path.

items.title: Z-loss regularization on logits
items.spec: Add an auxiliary z-loss term of 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) to the training loss to keep the logit normalizer near zero. Only the training objective changes, and the reported val_bpb evaluation stays untouched. This can improve numerical stability with the high LRs used here.

items.title: Dropout on residual branches
items.spec: Apply dropout with probability 0.05 to the outputs of the attention and MLP branches before they are added to the residual stream, active only during training. With roughly one pass over the data in 300 s, this is a small test that regularization does not hurt underfitting.

items.title: Lower Muon weight decay
items.spec: Reduce WEIGHT_DECAY for the Muon matrix parameters from 0.2 to 0.1. Keep the Adam groups unchanged. This tests whether the current decay is over-regularizing a short run that is still underfit.

items.title: Higher Muon weight decay
items.spec: Increase WEIGHT_DECAY for the Muon matrix parameters from 0.2 to 0.4. Keep the Adam groups unchanged. This tests the opposite direction in case the short run benefits from stronger regularization on weight norms.

items.title: Sequence length curriculum
items.spec: Train the first 25 percent of the time budget on sequences of half the current length with twice as many sequences per batch, keeping tokens per step fixed. Then switch to full length. This gives cheaper early attention and keeps the same total token count per step.

items.title: Longer training sequences
items.spec: Double the training sequence length while halving the number of sequences per batch so TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE in tokens is unchanged. Longer context may help bits-per-byte on the validation text. Keep the attention window pattern consistent with the new length.

items.title: Weight EMA for final model
items.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of the model weights with decay 0.999, updated after each optimizer step. Before training ends, copy the EMA weights into the model used for the final evaluation. Keep the training loop and the evaluation call unchanged otherwise.

items.title: Fused optimizers and TF32 matmuls
items.spec: Enable TF32 for matmuls and convolutions and set fused=True on the Adam optimizer groups. These are speed changes only, with no change to the math. The extra throughput within the fixed 300 s budget should lower val_bpb slightly.

items.title: Per-layer residual scale initialization
items.spec: Initialize the per-layer residual scaling scalars at 0.5 for the attention branch and 1.0 for the MLP branch instead of the current initialization. Keep them trained by the scalar Adam group at SCALAR_LR. This changes how much each block initially contributes to the residual stream.

items.title: Adam epsilon and beta1 for embeddings
items.spec: Set the Adam epsilon for the embedding and lm_head groups to 1e-10 and beta1 to 0.9 for those groups only, keeping ADAM_BETAS = (0.8, 0.95) for the scalar group. The high EMBEDDING_LR of 0.6 may need a smoother first-moment estimate. Only the embedding optimizer settings change.

items.title: Muon momentum warmup
items.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Leave all other Muon logic unchanged. This is a single change to how the momentum value is computed each step.

items.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations
items.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside Muon from 5 to 3 to save wall-clock time, which yields more optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s budget. Keep the coefficients and the rest of the update identical.

items.title: Remove cautious masking for Muon weight decay
items.spec: Replace the cautious weight decay (applied only where the update and parameter signs agree) with standard decoupled weight decay: p <- p*(1 - lr*WEIGHT_DECAY) applied to every Muon matrix parameter. Keep WEIGHT_DECAY at 0.2 and the rest of the optimizer unchanged.

items.title: Zero weight decay on embedding and LM head
items.spec: Exclude the token embedding and lm_head parameters from any weight decay (set their decay to 0) while keeping decay on matrix parameters as before. Implement by adding a per-group weight_decay field to the Adam parameter groups for embeddings and unembedding.

items.title: Small AdamW decay on scalar and Adam parameters
items.spec: Add a small decoupled weight decay of 0.01 to the Adam-optimized parameters (embeddings excluded), applied with the same learning-rate schedule as their Adam updates. Matrix parameters keep their current Muon handling.

items.title: Lower Adam epsilon
items.spec: Set the epsilon of all Adam optimizer groups to 1e-10 instead of the default 1e-8. This affects only the denominator stabilization in the Adam updates for embeddings, lm_head and scalars.

items.title: Matrix LR sweep upward
items.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05 with all other hyperparameters unchanged. The goal is to test whether the Muon matrix learning rate is currently too conservative for a 300 s run.

items.title: Unembedding LR sweep
items.spec: Change UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008 with all other hyperparameters unchanged, to test whether the lm_head is learning too slowly within the short training budget.

items.title: Longer warmdown
items.spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so that the learning rate decays over the final 70% of the time budget. Keep warmup at zero and all other settings unchanged.

items.title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear
items.spec: Replace the linear LR warmdown with a cosine decay from full LR to FINAL_LR_FRAC over the warmdown window, computed from the fraction of elapsed time. Apply the same multiplier to all optimizer groups as now.

items.title: Short warmup before constant LR
items.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the learning rate ramps linearly from 0 over the first 2% of the time budget before holding at full LR and then warming down. This protects the early steps of the large SCALAR_LR and EMBEDDING_LR settings.

items.title: Nonzero final learning-rate floor
items.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 so that the warmdown ends at 10% of the peak learning rate instead of zero. All other schedule parameters remain the same.

items.title: Linear decay of weight decay to zero
items.spec: Scale WEIGHT_DECAY by a factor that decreases linearly from 1 at the start of training to 0 at the end, based on elapsed time fraction. Recompute the effective decay each step while keeping the base value 0.2.

items.title: Value-embedding residual (ResFormer-style)
items.spec: Compute value vectors in every attention layer and mix in the first layer's value vectors through a learnable per-layer scalar added to the current layer's values before attention. Initialize the mixing scalar to zero so the model starts identical to the baseline.

items.title: Logit soft-capping
items.spec: Apply a soft cap to the output logits before the cross-entropy loss: logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15). Use the same scale for training and for the evaluation path as computed inside the model forward, without altering the evaluation call.

items.title: Deeper, narrower model
items.spec: Change DEPTH from 8 to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 48 so that model_dim = depth*aspect stays close to the baseline width while adding layers. Keep HEAD_DIM and all other settings unchanged, and check that the window pattern still matches the new depth.

items.title: Wider, shallower model
items.spec: Change DEPTH from 8 to 6 and ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 96 so the model is wider and shallower. Keep HEAD_DIM at 128 so the number of heads grows accordingly, and keep all other settings unchanged.

items.title: Full-context attention every other layer
items.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SLSL' so that half of the layers use full attention and the others use the half-context sliding window. This tests whether more global attention helps the short-sequence regime.

items.title: Squared-ReLU MLP activation
items.spec: Replace the MLP nonlinearity with relu(x)**2 in the feed-forward blocks, keeping hidden size and projections unchanged. This is a drop-in activation change with no added parameters.

items.title: Higher RoPE base frequency
items.spec: Increase the rotary embedding base from 10000 to 100000 so that positional frequencies vary more slowly over the sequence. Keep head dimension and all other attention code unchanged.

items.title: Per-head learnable QK scale
items.spec: After QK normalization, multiply queries and keys by a learnable per-head scalar initialized to 1, applied before the attention softmax. This allows each head to adapt its attention sharpness with negligible parameter cost.

items.title: Previous-token bigram mixing at input
items.spec: After the token embedding, add a learnable gate-weighted contribution from the previous token's embedding (shifted by one position, zero-padded at the start). Initialize the gate to zero so training starts from the baseline embedding behavior.

items.title: Per-layer residual scalars with zero-init output projections
items.spec: Make sure each block's attention and MLP output projection weights are zero-initialized and add a learnable per-layer residual scale initialized to 1, so every block starts as an identity mapping. Keep the existing per-layer scalars and their learning rate unchanged.

items.title: Smaller total batch for more steps
items.spec: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 tokens per optimizer step, with gradient accumulation adjusted so DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE stays 64. This doubles the number of optimizer updates in the fixed time budget.

items.title: Larger total batch with same LR
items.spec: Increase TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20 tokens per step, adjusting gradient accumulation so DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE stays at 64. Keep all learning rates unchanged to test whether lower gradient noise helps within the budget.

items.title: Z-loss regularization on logits
items.spec: Add an auxiliary z-loss term of 1e-4 times the squared log-sum-exp of the logits, averaged over tokens, to the training loss. This keeps logit magnitudes bounded and does not change the evaluation computation.

items.title: Exponential moving average of weights
items.spec: Maintain an EMA copy of the model parameters with decay 0.999 updated after each optimizer step, and copy the EMA weights into the model before the final training-state handoff to evaluation. The training forward and optimizer continue to use the live weights.

items.title: Gradient clipping
items.spec: Clip the global gradient norm to 1.0 before each optimizer step to guard against occasional spikes produced by the high Muon and scalar learning rates. Apply the clip to all trainable parameters.

items.title: Adam beta1 for scalars
items.spec: Set the first Adam beta (beta1) for the scalar parameter group to 0.9 while keeping beta2 at 0.95, and leave the other Adam groups on ADAM_BETAS. This tests whether a smoother momentum helps the per-layer scalars.

items.title: Polar Express orthogonalization coefficients
items.spec: Replace the fixed Newton-Schulz quintic coefficients inside Muon with the Polar Express per-iteration coefficient set for the same number of iterations. Keep the normalization and the learning-rate shape scaling unchanged.

items.title: Shape-aware Muon LR scaling
items.spec: Scale the Muon update for each matrix by max(1, rows/cols)**0.5 so that tall matrices receive a proportionally larger step, and remove any other shape factor in the current update. Keep MATRIX_LR at 0.04.

items.title: Compile and throughput tuning
items.spec: Enable fused or foreach implementations for the Adam and Muon steps and set torch.compile to mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' for the training step only, with the evaluation path untouched. The aim is more tokens processed in the fixed 300 s without changing the math.

items.title: Mixed-precision optimizer state
items.spec: Keep Muon momentum buffers in bfloat16 instead of float32 to reduce memory traffic and allow a larger effective step rate. Cast to float32 only inside the orthogonalization step, leaving parameters in their current dtype.
